translations.idiomatic: Mu Helin; Duan Yingju. (Corrupted wikisource fragment.)

sentences.zh: =楊捷=楊捷，字元凱，義州人，先世居寶應，明初，以軍功授後屯衛指揮使，世襲，遂家焉。

translations.literal: Yang Jie, style name Yuankai, was from Yizhou; his ancestors had lived in Baoying. At the beginning of the Ming, for military merit he was granted the post of Rear Garrison Guard commander, which was inherited in succession, and the family settled there.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jie, whose style was Yuankai, came from Yizhou. His forebears had lived in Baoying; in the early Ming a military merit award made them hereditary commanders of the Rear Garrison Guard, and the family made its home there.

sentences.zh: 捷初為明裨將，順治元年來降，授山西撫標中軍游擊。

translations.literal: Jie had first been a Ming deputy general; in the first year of Shunzhi he came over in surrender and was appointed mobile corps commander of the Shanxi governor-general's central army.
translations.idiomatic: Jie had begun as a Ming deputy general. In the first year of Shunzhi he surrendered and was made mobile corps commander of the Shanxi governor-general's central brigade.

sentences.zh: 嵐縣土寇高九英等聚眾剽掠，巡撫馬國柱檄捷捕治，斬九英，毀其巢。

translations.literal: The local bandits of Lan County, Gao Jiuying and others, gathered a crowd to plunder and raid; Grand Coordinator Ma Guozhu ordered Jie to capture and punish them; he beheaded Jiuying and destroyed their lair.
translations.idiomatic: When the Lan County bandit Gao Jiuying and his followers gathered to raid, Grand Coordinator Ma Guozhu ordered Jie to suppress them; Jie executed Jiuying and destroyed their stronghold.

sentences.zh: 國柱遷總督，以捷為督標中軍參將，旋擢副將。

translations.literal: When Guozhu was transferred to governor-general, he made Jie colonel of the governor-general's central army, and soon promoted him to deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: After Guozhu became governor-general, he appointed Jie colonel of his central brigade and soon promoted him to deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 四年，師定廣東，命捷率宣化、大同兵三千往鎮撫。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, after the army pacified Guangdong, Jie was ordered to lead three thousand troops from Xuanhua and Datong to garrison and pacify the region.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, once Guangdong had been pacified, he was ordered to take three thousand men from Xuanhua and Datong to garrison and calm the province.

sentences.zh: 五年，行次池州，金聲桓、李成棟叛。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, while marching and halting at Chizhou, Jin Shenghuan and Li Chengdong rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, as his column reached Chizhou, Jin Shenghuan and Li Chengdong rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 大將軍譚泰請以捷駐防九江會剿，即授九江總兵，率兵复都昌，獲聲桓所置吏餘應柱等，斬之。

translations.literal: Grand General Tan Tai requested that Jie garrison Jiujiang to join in suppression; he was at once made Jiujiang regional commander, led troops to recover Duchang, captured Yu Yingzhu and others, officials Jin Shenghuan had installed, and beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Tan Tai asked that Jie hold Jiujiang for the joint campaign; he was immediately made regional commander there, recovered Duchang, seized Jin Shenghuan's appointees such as Yu Yingzhu, and executed them.

sentences.zh: 江西平，敘功，予世職拖沙喇哈番。

translations.literal: When Jiangxi was pacified, merit was recorded and he was granted the hereditary rank of Tuo Shala Ha Fan.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiangxi was pacified, his service was recognized with the hereditary rank of Tuo Shala Ha Fan.

sentences.zh: 十年，從靖南將軍喀喀木討廣東叛鎮郝尚久，复潮州。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he followed Pacifier of the South General Kekemu to attack the rebel Guangdong garrison commander Hao Shangjiu and recovered Chaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he marched with Pacifier of the South General Kekemu against the rebel Guangdong commander Hao Shangjiu and retook Chaozhou.

sentences.zh: 調陝西興安，經略大學士洪承疇請留原鎮，加右都督。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Xing'an in Shaanxi; Grand Secretary Hong Chengchou, commissioner for pacification, asked that he remain at his former post, and he was given the additional title of Right Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Xing'an in Shaanxi, he was kept at his former post at Grand Secretary Hong Chengchou's request and promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 調福建隨徵右路總兵，十二年，敘复潮州功，進左都督。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Fujian's Right Route commander on the campaign staff; in the twelfth year, for recovering Chaozhou, merit was recorded and he was advanced to Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to command Fujian's right-route forces on campaign; in the twelfth year the retaking of Chaozhou was entered on the rolls and he rose to Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 鄭成功侵掠福建，與戰雲霄、銅山諸處，屢捷。

translations.literal: When Zheng Chenggong raided Fujian, he fought him at Yunxiao, Tongshan, and other places, winning repeated victories.
translations.idiomatic: As Zheng Chenggong harried Fujian, he met him in battle at Yunxiao, Tongshan, and elsewhere and won again and again.

sentences.zh: 十六年，擢江南提督。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was promoted to Jiangnan provincial commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was made provincial commander-in-chief of Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 會成功陷鎮江，窺江寧，加太子少保，充江南隨徵左路總兵，駐揚州，防江北要汛。

translations.literal: When Chenggong took Zhenjiang and threatened Jiangning, Jie was given the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, served as Jiangnan Left Route commander on the campaign staff, garrisoned Yangzhou, and guarded the key north-of-the-Yangtze river posts.
translations.idiomatic: When Chenggong seized Zhenjiang and menaced Nanjing, Jie was named Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, took command of Jiangnan's left-route campaign forces, garrisoned Yangzhou, and held the vital Yangtze crossings north of the river.

sentences.zh: 十八年，命署廬鳳提督，尋調山東。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was ordered to act as Luzhou-Fengyang provincial commander-in-chief, and soon transferred to Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was appointed acting commander-in-chief of Luzhou-Fengyang, then transferred to Shandong.

sentences.zh: 土寇於七敗竄入海，捷捕治其黨五十餘人，誅之。

translations.literal: The local bandit Yu Qibai fled into the sea after defeat; Jie captured and punished more than fifty of his followers and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit Yu Qibai, beaten, fled to sea; Jie rounded up more than fifty of his accomplices and put them to death.

sentences.zh: 康熙十二年，調江南。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Kangxi he was transferred to Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Kangxi he returned to Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 十七年，鄭錦攻漳州，陷海澄。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Zheng Jing attacked Zhangzhou and took Haicheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Zheng Jing struck at Zhangzhou and captured Haicheng.

sentences.zh: 調捷福建，轄水陸各軍，進少保兼太子太保。

translations.literal: Jie was transferred to Fujian to command all land and naval forces and was advanced to Junior Guardian and Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Jie was sent to Fujian to command both land and sea forces and promoted to Junior Guardian and Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「臣前勦賊雲霄、銅山間，深知閩兵不力戰。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "When I formerly suppressed bandits between Yunxiao and Tongshan, I came to know well that Fujian troops do not fight hard."
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he wrote: "When I campaigned earlier between Yunxiao and Tongshan, I learned how little fight there is in Fujian's native troops."

sentences.zh: 自任江南提督，召募材健，訓諫有年。

translations.literal: Since taking office as Jiangnan commander-in-chief, I have recruited sturdy men and trained and admonished them for years.
translations.idiomatic: Since I became Jiangnan commander-in-chief I have recruited able-bodied men and drilled them for years.

sentences.zh: 擬選三千人隨徵福建。

translations.literal: I propose to select three thousand men to follow the campaign to Fujian."
translations.idiomatic: I propose to take three thousand of them with me to Fujian."

sentences.zh: 」詔允之。

translations.literal: The edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved his request.

sentences.zh: 捷至福州，聞錦犯泉州，即督兵趨惠安。

translations.literal: When Jie reached Fuzhou and heard that Jing was attacking Quanzhou, he at once led troops toward Hui'an.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Fuzhou and learning that Jing was pressing Quanzhou, he marched immediately toward Hui'an.

sentences.zh: 錦將劉國軒斷洛陽橋，以三千人據陳山壩阻我師，捷遣游擊李璉等襲破之。

translations.literal: Jing's general Liu Guoxuan cut the Luoyang Bridge and with three thousand men held Chenshan Dam to block our army; Jie sent Mobile Corps Commander Li Lian and others to attack and break them.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's general Liu Guoxuan severed the Luoyang Bridge and blocked the road at Chenshan Dam with three thousand men; Jie sent Li Lian and other mobile commanders to storm and break the position.

sentences.zh: 總兵黃大來與副都統禪布等會師洛陽橋南夾擊，國軒遁，泉州平。

translations.literal: Regional Commander Huang Dalai and Vice Commander-in-Chief Chanbu and others joined forces south of Luoyang Bridge for a pincer attack; Guoxuan fled and Quanzhou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Huang Dalai, Vice Commander-in-Chief Chanbu, and others joined south of the Luoyang Bridge in a converging attack; Guoxuan fled and Quanzhou was secured.

sentences.zh: 錦將王一鵬复窺惠安，捷令總兵張韜御之，捕斬略盡。

translations.literal: Jing's general Wang Yipeng again threatened Hui'an; Jie ordered Regional Commander Zhang Tao to resist him and captured and beheaded nearly all of them.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing's general Wang Yipeng again menaced Hui'an, Jie had Regional Commander Zhang Tao meet him and killed or captured nearly the whole force.

sentences.zh: 其別將葉明、紀朝佐等出沒德化、永春間，蕭武等以舟師泊湄州，窺興化。

translations.literal: His other generals Ye Ming, Ji Chaozuo, and others appeared and vanished between Dehua and Yongchun; Xiao Wu and others anchored a fleet at Meizhou and threatened Xinghua.
translations.idiomatic: Other commanders such as Ye Ming and Ji Chaozuo raided between Dehua and Yongchun, while Xiao Wu moored a fleet off Meizhou and eyed Xinghua.

sentences.zh: 捷遣將防守策應，移師至漳州。

translations.literal: Jie sent generals to defend and coordinate support, then moved his army to Zhangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jie detached officers to hold the line and coordinate relief, then shifted his main force to Zhangzhou.

sentences.zh: 偕副都統吉爾塔布等敗國軒於江東橋，又分兵屯守柯坑山、鳳山、萬松關諸要隘，遣別將扼守榴山寨。

translations.literal: Together with Vice Commander-in-Chief Jiertabu and others he defeated Guoxuan at Jiangdong Bridge, then divided troops to garrison the passes at Kekeng Hill, Feng Hill, Wansong Pass, and other key points, and sent other generals to hold Liushan Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: With Vice Commander-in-Chief Jiertabu and others he routed Guoxuan at Jiangdong Bridge, posted detachments at Kekeng Hill, Feng Hill, Wansong Pass, and other choke points, and sent subordinates to hold Liushan Stockade.

sentences.zh: 捷初上官，疏請別設水師提督，得以專禦陸路。

translations.literal: When Jie first took office he memorialized asking that a separate naval commander-in-chief be established so that he might devote himself solely to land defense.
translations.idiomatic: On first taking command he asked that a separate naval commander-in-chief be appointed so he could focus on land operations.

sentences.zh: 上授捷昭武將軍，領福建陸路提督事。

translations.literal: The emperor appointed Jie General Who Pacifies Wu and charged him with Fujian land forces as provincial commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: The throne named him General Who Pacifies Wu and put him in charge of Fujian's land forces as provincial commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 十八年，國軒率眾劫榴山寨，欲奪江東橋。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Guoxuan led a force to raid Liushan Stockade, intending to seize Jiangdong Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year Guoxuan struck at Liushan Stockade, aiming to retake Jiangdong Bridge.

sentences.zh: 捷會平南將軍賚塔等分兩翼夾擊，大敗之於下坑山及歐溪頭，斬級千餘，獲甲仗無算。

translations.literal: Jie joined Pacifier of the South General Baita and others in a two-wing pincer, inflicting a great defeat at Xiakeng Hill and Ouxi Head, beheading more than a thousand, and capturing armor and weapons beyond count.
translations.idiomatic: With Pacifier of the South General Baita he attacked from both wings and crushed the enemy at Xiakeng Hill and Ouxi Head, taking more than a thousand heads and countless arms and armor.

sentences.zh: 國軒屯獅子山，聯絡遠近各寨為聲援。

translations.literal: Guoxuan encamped on Lion Hill and linked nearby and distant stockades for mutual support.
translations.idiomatic: Guoxuan held Lion Hill and coordinated stockades near and far as a support network.

sentences.zh: 十九年，捷親率健卒剿平烏嶼諸寨，與總督姚啟聖、總兵姚大來等分下玉洲、三汊、石碼，連破十九寨，進取海澄。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year Jie personally led picked troops to suppress and pacify the stockades of Wuyu and elsewhere; with Governor-General Yao Qisheng, Regional Commander Yao Dalai, and others he divided forces to descend on Yuzhou, Sancha, and Shima, broke nineteen stockades in succession, and advanced on Haicheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he led elite troops in person to clear the Wuyu stockades; with Governor-General Yao Qisheng and Regional Commander Yao Dalai he sent columns against Yuzhou, Sancha, and Shima, took nineteen stockades in a row, and pressed on Haicheng.

sentences.zh: 錦將蘇侃以城降，遂乘勝與浙江提督石調聲复廈門，國軒自銅山竄歸台灣。

translations.literal: Jing's general Su Kan surrendered the city; pressing the advantage, together with Zhejiang Commander-in-Chief Shi Tiaosheng he recovered Xiamen, and Guoxuan fled from Tongshan back to Taiwan.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing's general Su Kan surrendered the city, Jie pressed the victory and, with Zhejiang commander Shi Tiaosheng, retook Xiamen; Guoxuan fled from Tongshan to Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 是年，以老病乞罷，命還任江南提督。

translations.literal: That year, citing age and illness, he asked to retire; he was ordered to return to his post as Jiangnan commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: That year he pleaded age and illness to resign and was sent back to his Jiangnan command.

sentences.zh: 敘复海澄功，進世職三等阿達哈哈番。

translations.literal: For recovering Haicheng, merit was recorded and his hereditary rank was advanced to third-class Ada Ha Ha Fan.
translations.idiomatic: The retaking of Haicheng was entered on the rolls and his hereditary rank rose to third-class Ada Ha Ha Fan.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，卒，年七十四，贈少傅兼太子太傅，諡敏壯。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year he died at seventy-four; he was posthumously given Junior Tutor and Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous title Minzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the thirty-ninth year at seventy-four, was posthumously honored as Junior Tutor and Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and received the temple name Minzhuang.

sentences.zh: 孫鑄，襲職，請改籍揚州衛。

translations.literal: His grandson Zhu inherited the office and requested transfer of household registration to Yangzhou Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Zhu inherited the rank and asked to have the family's register moved to Yangzhou Guard.

sentences.zh: =石調聲=石調聲，漢​​軍鑲黃旗人。

translations.literal: Shi Tiaosheng, a Han Bannerman of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Tiaosheng belonged to the Han Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 以佐領從征廣東，敘功，予世職拖沙喇哈番。

translations.literal: As an assistant commandant he followed the Guangdong campaign; merit was recorded and he was granted the hereditary rank of Tuo Shala Ha Fan.
translations.idiomatic: Serving as an assistant commandant on the Guangdong campaign, he earned the hereditary rank of Tuo Shala Ha Fan.

sentences.zh: 遷參領，駐防福建。

translations.literal: He was transferred to deputy commandant and garrisoned in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to deputy commandant, he was posted to garrison Fujian.

sentences.zh: 擢杭州副都統。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice commander-in-chief at Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice commander-in-chief at Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 耿精忠犯浙江，調聲迎擊，屢卻賊。

translations.literal: When Geng Jingzhong invaded Zhejiang, Tiaosheng met the attack and repeatedly repelled the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When Geng Jingzhong struck into Zhejiang, Tiaosheng met him in the field and drove the rebels back again and again.

sentences.zh: 擢浙江提督。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Zhejiang provincial commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was made provincial commander-in-chief of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 康熙十七年，鄭錦遣劉國軒等犯海澄，詔趣調聲赴援，未至而海澄陷，康親王檄守惠安。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Kangxi, Zheng Jing sent Liu Guoxuan and others against Haicheng; an edict urged Tiaosheng to hurry to the relief, but before he arrived Haicheng fell, and Prince Kang ordered him to hold Hui'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Kangxi, Zheng Jing sent Liu Guoxuan against Haicheng; the court ordered Tiaosheng to hurry south, but Haicheng fell before he arrived and Prince Kang directed him to hold Hui'an.

sentences.zh: 賊陷同安，遂圍泉州，惠安亦陷。

translations.literal: The rebels took Tong'an, then besieged Quanzhou, and Hui'an also fell.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels captured Tong'an, laid siege to Quanzhou, and Hui'an fell as well.

sentences.zh: 調聲退軍興化，與參贊大臣禪布攻复惠安，逐北至洛陽橋。

translations.literal: Tiaosheng withdrew to Xinghua, and with Adviser Chanbu recovered Hui'an and pursued north to Luoyang Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Tiaosheng fell back to Xinghua; with Adviser Chanbu he retook Hui'an and pursued the enemy north to the Luoyang Bridge.

sentences.zh: 泉州圍解。

translations.literal: The siege of Quanzhou was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: The siege of Quanzhou was broken.

sentences.zh: 复偕副都統沃申破賊江東橋。

translations.literal: He again joined Vice Commander-in-Chief Woshen to defeat the rebels at Jiangdong Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: He again joined Vice Commander-in-Chief Woshen to rout the rebels at Jiangdong Bridge.

sentences.zh: 頃之，國軒等復奪橋，斷餉道，將軍賚塔檄調聲迎擊，敗之。

translations.literal: Shortly after, Guoxuan and others retook the bridge and cut the supply route; General Baita ordered Tiaosheng to meet the attack and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Guoxuan retook the bridge and severed the supply line; General Baita ordered Tiaosheng forward and he beat them back.

sentences.zh: 十九年，复廈門、金門，國軒遁。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he recovered Xiamen and Kinmen; Guoxuan fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year Xiamen and Kinmen were retaken and Guoxuan fled.

sentences.zh: 調聲還浙江任。

translations.literal: Tiaosheng returned to his Zhejiang post.
translations.idiomatic: Tiaosheng went back to his Zhejiang command.

sentences.zh: 初賊陷江山、惠安，戰士暴骨多未瘞，議者以咎調聲。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the rebels took Jiangshan and Hui'an, many soldiers' bones lay exposed unburied; critics blamed Tiaosheng.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels had taken Jiangshan and Hui'an, many dead were left unburied; critics held Tiaosheng responsible.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，追論奪官及世職。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was retrospectively judged and stripped of office and hereditary rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year a retrospective inquiry stripped him of office and hereditary rank.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: He soon died.
translations.idiomatic: He died not long after.

sentences.zh: =萬正色=萬正色，字惟高，福建晉江人。

translations.literal: Wan Zhengse, style name Weigao, was from Jinjiang in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Zhengse, whose style was Weigao, came from Jinjiang in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 少入伍。

translations.literal: In youth he entered military service.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the army in his youth.

sentences.zh: 以招降海寇陳燦等，敘功，授陝西興安游擊。

translations.literal: For inducing the surrender of sea bandits such as Chen Can, merit was recorded and he was appointed mobile corps commander at Xing'an in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: For winning over sea bandits such as Chen Can, he was rewarded with appointment as mobile corps commander at Xing'an in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 康熙十二年，吳三桂反，正色從西安將軍瓦爾喀徵四川。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Kangxi, when Wu Sangui rebelled, Zhengse followed Xi'an General Wuerka on the Sichuan campaign.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sangui rose in the twelfth year of Kangxi, Zhengse marched to Sichuan under Xi'an General Wuerka.

sentences.zh: 叛將譚弘等據陽平關拒戰，敗之於野狐嶺，乘勝复廣元、昭化。

translations.literal: The rebel general Tan Hong and others held Yangping Pass to resist; he defeated them at Yehu Ridge and, pressing the victory, recovered Guangyuan and Zhaohua.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel general Tan Hong held Yangping Pass; Zhengse beat him at Yehu Ridge and, pressing on, retook Guangyuan and Zhaohua.

sentences.zh: 累擢岳州水師總兵。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to regional commander of the Yuezhou naval forces.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to command the Yuezhou naval forces as regional commander.

sentences.zh: 時三桂據岳州，扼守洞庭湖套，植木為椿阻我師。

translations.literal: At that time Sangui held Yuezhou, guarded the Dongting lake bend, and planted timbers as stakes to block our army.
translations.idiomatic: Sangui then held Yuezhou, blocked the Dongting narrows, and drove wooden stakes into the channel to stop imperial boats.

sentences.zh: 十七年，正色上官，率舟師夜入亂葦中，拔椿盡，擊賊，屢敗之。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, when Zhengse took office, he led the fleet by night into the tangled reeds, pulled up all the stakes, attacked the rebels, and defeated them repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, on taking command, he led his fleet by night through the reed beds, cleared every stake, and beat the rebels again and again.

sentences.zh: 三桂將江義、巴養元、杜輝等率舟二百攻柳林嘴，正色與游擊唐善等擊之，毀其舟。

translations.literal: Sangui's generals Jiang Yi, Ba Yangyuan, Du Hui, and others led two hundred boats to attack Liulin Mouth; Zhengse with Mobile Corps Commander Tang Shan and others met them and destroyed their vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Sangui's generals Jiang Yi, Ba Yangyuan, and Du Hui brought two hundred boats against Liulin Mouth; Zhengse and Tang Shan smashed the fleet.

sentences.zh: 是歲三桂死於衡州，其子應麒與輝、義等守岳州。

translations.literal: That year Sangui died at Hengzhou; his son Yinglin with Hui, Yi, and others held Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: That year Sangui died at Hengzhou; his son Yinglin, with Hui, Yi, and others, still held Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 正色遣千總魏士曾齎書十四分致應麒部將，士曾為所殺，應麒亦殺部將之受書者，遂內訌。

translations.literal: Zhengse sent Battalion Commander Wei Shizeng with fourteen copies of a letter to Yinglin's subordinate generals; Shizeng was killed, and Yinglin also killed the generals who had received the letters, and thus internal strife arose.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengse sent Battalion Commander Wei Shizeng with fourteen copies of a letter to Yinglin's officers; the rebels killed Shizeng, Yinglin executed the officers who had taken the letters, and the garrison turned on itself.

sentences.zh: 其將陳華、李超、王度衝出降，應麒棄城遁，遂復岳州。

translations.literal: His generals Chen Hua, Li Chao, and Wang Duchong came out to surrender; Yinglin abandoned the city and fled, and Yuezhou was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Generals Chen Hua, Li Chao, and Wang Duchong defected; Yinglin fled the city and Yuezhou was retaken.

sentences.zh: 正色為士曾請卹，贈守備。

translations.literal: Zhengse requested mourning grants for Shizeng and had him posthumously given the rank of garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengse sought compensation for Shizeng and had him posthumously honored as garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 十八年，追敘克陽平關功，加左都督。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, for merit in taking Yangping Pass, he was retrospectively recorded and given the additional title Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year the capture of Yangping Pass was belatedly recognized and he was named Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 大將軍康親王杰書徵福建，耿精忠降，而鄭錦猶踞金門、廈門，陷海澄。

translations.literal: Grand General Prince Kang Jieshu campaigned in Fujian; Geng Jingzhong surrendered, but Zheng Jing still held Kinmen and Xiamen and had taken Haicheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand General Prince Kang Jieshu marched on Fujian, Geng Jingzhong submitted, but Zheng Jing still held Kinmen and Xiamen and had seized Haicheng.

sentences.zh: 正色自以閩人習海上事狀，因陳水陸戰守機宜，言：「福建負山枕海，賊踪出沒靡常。

translations.literal: Zhengse, as a Fujian native familiar with maritime affairs, therefore set forth the essentials of land and sea offense and defense, saying: "Fujian rests on mountains and faces the sea; the rebels' tracks appear and vanish without fixed pattern."
translations.idiomatic: As a Fujian man who knew the coast, he laid out how land and sea forces should fight and hold ground: "Fujian lies against mountains and the sea; rebel movements are never predictable."

sentences.zh: 宜擇官兵習於陸者分佈要害，使賊不得登岸；

translations.literal: One should choose officers and troops skilled on land and distribute them at key points so that the rebels cannot come ashore;
translations.idiomatic: Post troops trained for land fighting at the key points so the rebels cannot land;

sentences.zh: 水軍自萬安鎮順流直下金門，塞海澄以斷其歸路。

translations.literal: the naval force should descend with the current from Wan'an Town straight to Kinmen and block Haicheng to cut off their line of retreat."
translations.idiomatic: send the fleet downriver from Wan'an toward Kinmen and seal Haicheng to cut their retreat."

sentences.zh: 賊自廈門來援，則從金門掩擊。

translations.literal: If the rebels come from Xiamen to relieve them, strike from Kinmen in ambush.
translations.idiomatic: If they send relief from Xiamen, fall on them from Kinmen.

sentences.zh: 更請蠲除沿海邊地雜派，設法招撫，善為安置，則賊黨自散。

translations.literal: He further asked to remit miscellaneous levies on coastal border districts, devise means to win over and pacify people, and settle them well, then rebel bands would scatter of themselves."
translations.idiomatic: He also urged remitting miscellaneous coastal levies, winning people over, and settling them properly so rebel bands would melt away."

sentences.zh: 」疏入，詔加太子少保，調福建水師總兵，擢提督。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, an edict added Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, transferred him to Fujian naval regional commander, and promoted him to provincial commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was approved: he was named Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, made Fujian naval regional commander, and promoted to provincial commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 時議檄調荷蘭國船進取廈門，正色疏言：「荷蘭船遲速莫必，延至三四月，風信轉南，即難前進。

translations.literal: At the time it was proposed to order Dutch ships to advance on Xiamen; Zhengse memorialized: "Dutch ships may be fast or slow and cannot be relied on; if delayed until the third or fourth month, when the wind turns south, advance will be difficult."
translations.idiomatic: Some proposed calling in Dutch ships to take Xiamen; Zhengse objected: "Dutch sailing is uncertain—wait until the third or fourth month and the south wind will make advance impossible."

sentences.zh: 今新舊鳥船俱集，臣與撫臣吳興祚決計進討，臣率水師直攻海壇，興祚率陸兵為聲援。

translations.literal: Now old and new bird-ships are all assembled; the Grand Coordinator Wu Xingzuo and I have resolved to advance; I shall lead the naval force straight against Haitan, and Xingzuo shall lead land troops as a supporting demonstration."
translations.idiomatic: Our bird-ships old and new are ready; Grand Coordinator Wu Xingzuo and I have decided to attack—I will strike Haitan by sea while Xingzuo moves on land in support."

sentences.zh: 十九年，正色徵海壇，分前鋒為六隊，親統巨艦繼之，又以輕舟繞出左右，並力夾攻，發砲擊沈敵艦，溺死三千餘人，遂取海壇。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year Zhengse campaigned against Haitan, divided the vanguard into six columns, personally commanded great ships to follow, and also sent light boats to circle left and right; attacking together from both sides, he fired cannon and sank enemy vessels, drowning more than three thousand men, and thus took Haitan.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he attacked Haitan with six vanguard squadrons, followed in his flagship, and sent light craft around both flanks; converging fire sank enemy ships and drowned more than three thousand men, and Haitan fell.

sentences.zh: 其將硃天貴遁，正色追躡至平海澳，天貴走崇武，正色掩擊，大敗之。

translations.literal: His general Zhu Tiangui fled; Zhengse pursued to Pinghai Bay; Tiangui ran to Chongwu; Zhengse struck in ambush and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: When his general Zhu Tiangui fled, Zhengse chased him to Pinghai Bay; Tiangui ran on to Chongwu, where Zhengse ambushed and routed him.

sentences.zh: 與將軍拉哈達、總督姚啟聖、巡撫吳興祚、提督楊捷會師取廈門，天貴降。

translations.literal: Together with General Lahada, Governor-General Yao Qisheng, Grand Coordinator Wu Xingzuo, and Commander-in-Chief Yang Jie he united forces to take Xiamen; Tiangui surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Joining General Lahada, Governor-General Yao Qisheng, Grand Coordinator Wu Xingzuo, and Commander Yang Jie, he retook Xiamen and Tiangui submitted.

sentences.zh: 錦竄歸台灣。

translations.literal: Jing fled back to Taiwan.
translations.idiomatic: Jing fled to Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 疏請分兵鎮守濱海要地，上遣兵部侍郎溫岱蒞視。

translations.literal: He memorialized asking to divide troops to garrison key coastal points; the emperor sent Vice Minister of War Wen Dai to inspect on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to garrison the main coastal points in detachments; the throne sent Vice Minister of War Wen Dai to survey the coast.

sentences.zh: 尋議銅山、廈門諸處量設總兵以下官，留水師二萬人分鎮之。

translations.literal: Soon it was decided to establish regional commanders and subordinate officers at Tongshan, Xiamen, and other places as appropriate, leaving twenty thousand naval troops distributed in garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: It was then agreed to post regional commanders and subordinates at Tongshan, Xiamen, and elsewhere and to keep twenty thousand naval troops in coastal garrisons.

sentences.zh: 初，海壇既克，下兵部敘功。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Haitan was taken, the matter was sent down to the Ministry of War to record merit.
translations.idiomatic: After Haitan fell, the Ministry of War was ordered to record rewards.

sentences.zh: 啟聖語溫岱：「正色先與天貴約乃進兵，未嘗與賊戰。

translations.literal: Qisheng told Wen Dai: "Zhengse first made an agreement with Tiangui and only then advanced; he never actually fought the rebels."
translations.idiomatic: Qisheng told Wen Dai that Zhengse had arranged matters with Tiangui before advancing and had never really fought the enemy.

sentences.zh: 」兵部疏聞，上命仍議敘，予世職拜他喇布勒哈番。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War memorialized the report; the emperor ordered that merit still be recorded and granted the hereditary rank of Baitala Bule Ha Fan.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War reported this, but the emperor ordered rewards to proceed anyway and granted the hereditary rank of Baitala Bule Ha Fan.

sentences.zh: 上諭正色規取台灣，正色請緩師。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed Zhengse to plan the recovery of Taiwan; Zhengse asked to delay the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told him to plan the reconquest of Taiwan; Zhengse asked for more time.

sentences.zh: 二十年，改陸路提督。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was changed to land forces provincial commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he was transferred to command land forces.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，調雲南。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was transferred to Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he was posted to Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 未幾，與鶴慶總兵王珍互訐，命與珍詣京師質問。

translations.literal: Before long he and Heqing Regional Commander Wang Zhen accused each other; both were ordered to come to the capital for examination.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he and Heqing commander Wang Zhen traded accusations; both were summoned to the capital to answer charges.

sentences.zh: 總督范承勳劾正色納賄侵蝕，上遣侍郎多奇、傅拉塔按治，下刑部論死，上以正色功多，特宥之，奪官，仍留世職。

translations.literal: Governor-General Fan Chengxun impeached Zhengse for taking bribes and embezzlement; the emperor sent Vice Ministers Duoqi and Fulata to investigate; the Ministry of Punishments judged death, but because Zhengse's merits were many the emperor specially pardoned him, stripped office, yet retained hereditary rank.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Fan Chengxun charged him with bribery and graft; Vice Ministers Duoqi and Fulata were sent to investigate; the Ministry of Punishments recommended death, but the emperor spared him for his long service, removed his office, and let him keep his hereditary rank.

sentences.zh: 三十年，卒。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the thirtieth year.

sentences.zh: =吳英=吳英，字為高，福建莆田人。

translations.literal: Wu Ying, style name Weigao, was from Putian in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Ying, whose style was Weigao, came from Putian in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 幼為海賊掠置島中，更姓王。

translations.literal: In childhood he was seized by sea pirates and placed on an island, and his surname was changed to Wang.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was taken by pirates to an island and given the surname Wang.

sentences.zh: 康熙二年，赴泉州降，授守備劄。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kangxi he went to Quanzhou to surrender and was given a garrison commander's commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kangxi he surrendered at Quanzhou and was commissioned as garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 從提督王進功攻鄭錦，拔銅山城，加都司僉書銜。

translations.literal: He followed Commander-in-Chief Wang Jingong in attacking Zheng Jing, took Tongshan city, and was given the additional title of vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Serving under Commander Wang Jingong against Zheng Jing, he captured Tongshan and was given vice director of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 尋授浙江提標都司。

translations.literal: He was soon appointed director of the Zhejiang commander-in-chief's guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made director of the Zhejiang commander's guard.

sentences.zh: 十三年，耿精忠反，其將曾養性侵浙，總兵祖弘勳以溫州叛應之，分犯寧波、紹興。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Geng Jingzhong rebelled; his general Zeng Yangxing invaded Zhejiang, and Regional Commander Zu Hongxun rebelled at Wenzhou in response, dividing forces to attack Ningbo and Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Geng Jingzhong rose; his general Zeng Yangxing struck into Zhejiang while Zu Hongxun rebelled at Wenzhou and sent columns against Ningbo and Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 英從提督塞白理擊敗之，降其將李榮春等，遷左營游擊。

translations.literal: Ying followed Commander-in-Chief Saibaili in defeating them, induced the surrender of their generals Li Rongchun and others, and was transferred to Left Camp mobile corps commander.
translations.idiomatic: With Commander Saibaili he routed the rebels, won over Li Rongchun and other generals, and was made Left Camp mobile commander.

sentences.zh: 十四年，養性、弘勳率眾十餘萬犯台州。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Yangxing and Hongxun led more than a hundred thousand men against Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year Yangxing and Hongxun brought more than a hundred thousand men against Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 英言於塞白理，陽修毛坪山徑，潛引兵間道自仙居襲賊後，賊踞黃岩半山嶺拒戰。

translations.literal: Ying said to Saibaili that they should openly repair the Maoping Hill path while secretly leading troops by a byway from Xianju to strike the rebels from behind; the rebels held Ban Shan Ridge at Huangyan to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Ying advised Saibaili to repair the Maoping Hill road openly while sending a column secretly from Xianju to hit the enemy's rear; the rebels held Ban Shan Ridge at Huangyan.

sentences.zh: 英偕游擊曾承等冒矢石前進，斬其將劉邦仁等，遂復黃岩，遷中軍參將。

translations.literal: Ying with Mobile Corps Commander Zeng Cheng and others advanced under arrow and stone fire, beheaded their general Liu Bangren and others, recovered Huangyan, and was transferred to central army colonel.
translations.idiomatic: Ying and Zeng Cheng pressed forward under fire, killed Liu Bangren and other commanders, retook Huangyan, and he was promoted to central army colonel.

sentences.zh: 十五年，貝子傅拉塔規復溫州，養性、弘勳率三萬人乘夜劫營。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Prince Fulata planned to recover Wenzhou; Yangxing and Hongxun led thirty thousand men to raid the camp by night.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year Prince Fulata planned the recovery of Wenzhou; Yangxing and Hongxun led thirty thousand men in a night attack on the camp.

sentences.zh: 英分兵五百伏賊後，自率精銳據大羊山，阻其要道，遇賊，殊死戰，身中數槍。

translations.literal: Ying detached five hundred men to lie in ambush behind the rebels, personally led picked troops to hold Dayang Hill and block their vital route, met the enemy in desperate battle, and was struck by several spears.
translations.idiomatic: Ying posted five hundred men in the enemy's rear, held Dayang Hill with elite troops to block their line of march, fought hand to hand when they came up, and took several spear wounds.

sentences.zh: 師繼進，伏盡起，賊大潰，斬獲無算。

translations.literal: The army pressed on, the ambush forces all rose, the rebels collapsed in great disorder, and heads and captives were beyond count.
translations.idiomatic: The main force advanced, the ambush closed in, the rebels broke completely, and the slaughter and captures were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 尋從提督石調聲援象山，賊屯石門、西溪二嶺。

translations.literal: Soon he followed Commander-in-Chief Shi Tiaosheng to relieve Xiangshan; the rebels encamped on Shimen and Xixi ridges.
translations.idiomatic: He soon marched with Commander Shi Tiaosheng to relieve Xiangshan, where rebels held Shimen and Xixi ridges.

sentences.zh: 英偕游擊侯奇等分兵三道抵慈谿，擊沈賊船，殲其眾，遂復象山。

translations.literal: Ying with Mobile Corps Commander Hou Qi and others divided into three columns to reach Cixi, sank rebel boats, annihilated their force, and recovered Xiangshan.
translations.idiomatic: With Hou Qi he split into three columns toward Cixi, sank rebel ships, destroyed the enemy, and retook Xiangshan.

sentences.zh: 九月，康親王杰書進徵福建，精忠降，養性、弘勳引退。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Prince Kang Jieshu advanced into Fujian; Jingzhong surrendered and Yangxing and Hongxun withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Prince Kang marched into Fujian; Jingzhong submitted and Yangxing and Hongxun pulled back.

sentences.zh: 其將馮公輔猶踞松陽，英入山，招之降。

translations.literal: Their general Feng Gongfu still held Songyang; Ying entered the mountains and induced him to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Their general Feng Gongfu still held Songyang; Ying went into the hills and won him over.

sentences.zh: 其黨林惟仁等屯處州，英剿撫兼用，斬賊五百餘，降惟仁及兵千餘。

translations.literal: Their faction, Lin Weiren and others, encamped at Chuzhou; Ying used suppression and pacification together, beheaded more than five hundred rebels, and induced Weiren and more than a thousand troops to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Weiren and his band held Chuzhou; Ying combined force and persuasion, killed more than five hundred rebels, and won over Weiren and a thousand men.

sentences.zh: 十七年，錦犯泉州，康親王檄調聲赴援，英率師從。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Jing attacked Quanzhou; Prince Kang ordered Tiaosheng to hurry to the relief, and Ying led troops to follow.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Jing struck at Quanzhou; Prince Kang summoned Shi Tiaosheng south and Ying marched with him.

sentences.zh: 錦將劉國軒據洛陽橋，英自上游陳山壩渡江，以奇兵出賊後，造浮橋濟師，前後夾攻，斬級六百有奇。

translations.literal: Jing's general Liu Guoxuan held Luoyang Bridge; Ying crossed the river from upstream at Chenshan Dam, sent a surprise force behind the rebels, built a pontoon bridge to ferry troops, attacked front and rear, and beheaded more than six hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's Liu Guoxuan held the Luoyang Bridge; Ying crossed upstream at Chenshan Dam, sent a flanking force to the enemy's rear, threw a pontoon bridge across, attacked from both sides, and took more than six hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 遷福建督標中軍副將。

translations.literal: He was transferred to deputy commander of the Fujian governor-general's central army.
translations.idiomatic: He was made deputy commander of the Fujian governor-general's central brigade.

sentences.zh: 率師援漳州，連克十九寨，轉戰至江口，發砲擊沈敵船，遂復海澄。

translations.literal: He led troops to relieve Zhangzhou, took nineteen stockades in succession, fought on to Jiangkou, fired cannon and sank enemy vessels, and recovered Haicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Leading the relief of Zhangzhou, he stormed nineteen stockades in a row, fought to Jiangkou, sank enemy ships by cannon fire, and retook Haicheng.

sentences.zh: 十八年，國軒复擁眾數万屯郭塘、歐溪頭，謀奪江東橋，英擊走之，擢同安總兵。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Guoxuan again gathered tens of thousands at Guotang and Ouxi Head, plotting to seize Jiangdong Bridge; Ying attacked and drove him off and was promoted to Tong'an regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year Guoxuan massed tens of thousands at Guotang and Ouxi Head to retake Jiangdong Bridge; Ying drove him off and was made regional commander of Tong'an.

sentences.zh: 十九年，偕寧海將軍拉哈達、巡撫吳興祚自同安港口分兵，進克廈門，錦遁歸台灣。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, together with Pacifier of the Sea General Lahada and Grand Coordinator Wu Xingzuo, he divided forces from Tong'an harbor and advanced to take Xiamen; Jing fled back to Taiwan.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he joined General Lahada and Grand Coordinator Wu Xingzuo in a landing from Tong'an harbor, retook Xiamen, and Jing fled to Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 是年英奏請復姓。

translations.literal: That year Ying memorialized asking to restore his original surname.
translations.idiomatic: That year he asked the throne to restore his family name.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，移興化，會施琅進攻澎湖。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was moved to Xinghua and joined Shi Lang in the attack on Penghu.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he was posted to Xinghua and took part in Shi Lang's assault on Penghu.

sentences.zh: 英偕總兵硃天貴、林賢等自八罩嶼乘風進擊，游擊藍理陷圍，英衝入敵陣，拔之出。

translations.literal: Ying with Regional Commanders Zhu Tiangui, Lin Xian, and others sailed from Bazhao Islet with the wind to attack; Mobile Corps Commander Lan Li was surrounded, and Ying charged into the enemy line and pulled him out.
translations.idiomatic: With Zhu Tiangui and Lin Xian he sailed from Bazhao Islet before the wind; when Lan Li was surrounded, Ying broke into the enemy ranks and brought him out.

sentences.zh: 翌日，進取虎井嶼，英右耳中槍，益力戰，躍入敵艦，手刃其將鄭仁，餘悉駭竄。

translations.literal: The next day they advanced on Hujing Islet; Ying was struck in the right ear by a musket ball, fought all the harder, leaped onto an enemy vessel, and personally killed their general Zheng Ren; the rest fled in terror.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they took Hujing Islet; a musket ball pierced Ying's right ear, but he fought harder, boarded an enemy ship, killed Zheng Ren with his own hand, and the rest scattered in panic.

sentences.zh: 國軒與鄭克塽乞降，事具瑯傳。

translations.literal: Guoxuan and Zheng Keshuang begged to surrender; the affair is recorded in Lang's biography.
translations.idiomatic: Guoxuan and Zheng Keshuang sued for peace; the full account is in Shi Lang's biography.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，入覲，奏言：「台灣地勢絕險，土番止求衣食，素無他原。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he came to court and memorialized: "Taiwan's terrain is extremely perilous; the native tribes seek only food and clothing and ordinarily have no other designs."
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he presented himself at court and said: "Taiwan's terrain is forbidding; the aborigines want only food and clothing and as a rule harbor no other aims."

sentences.zh: 自來小寇竊發，皆由內地奸民作崇，陸師搜捕易盡。

translations.literal: Whenever small bandits have arisen in secret, it has always been because mainland traitors stirred them up; land forces can search them out and finish them easily.
translations.idiomatic: Petty raids have always been stirred up by mainland collaborators; land troops can hunt them down easily.

sentences.zh: 前議設水師趕繒雙篷船百，請減十之八，留二十船分撥台灣、澎湖二處，傳遞文書。

translations.literal: It was earlier proposed to establish a hundred double-sailed naval courier boats; he asked to reduce this by eight-tenths and keep twenty boats divided between Taiwan and Penghu for dispatching documents.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred double-sailed courier boats had been proposed; he asked to cut that to twenty, split between Taiwan and Penghu for carrying dispatches.

sentences.zh: 台灣、澎湖經制官兵一萬員名，前議以鹿皮、白糖通洋助餉，不能如期給發。

translations.literal: The ten thousand regular troops of Taiwan and Penghu were earlier to be supported by trading deerskins and sugar overseas, but payment could not be issued on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: The ten thousand garrison troops on Taiwan and Penghu were to be paid from overseas trade in deerskins and sugar, but the money never arrived on time.

sentences.zh: 臣見台灣民田之外，別有水田，俱屬鄭氏親黨及其部將，耕牛甚多。

translations.literal: Your servant has seen that besides civilian fields in Taiwan there are separate paddy fields, all belonging to the Zheng clan's kin and their subordinate generals, with many draft oxen.
translations.idiomatic: I have found that besides civilian land in Taiwan there are paddy fields held by the Zheng clan and their officers, with many oxen.

sentences.zh: 請分四千屯田，每兵給田三十畝、牛一，課耕種。

translations.literal: He asked to assign four thousand men to garrison farming, giving each soldier thirty mu of land and one ox, and requiring cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed putting four thousand troops on garrison farms, thirty mu and one ox per man, with compulsory cultivation.

sentences.zh: 農隙操練，則兵有恆產，餉可省半。

translations.literal: Drilling in the intervals of farming, the troops would have fixed property and rations could be cut by half."
translations.idiomatic: Training between seasons would give the men a livelihood and cut the ration bill in half."

sentences.zh: 」疏入，命議行。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, he was ordered to deliberate and implement it.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was approved for implementation.

sentences.zh: 尋移鎮浙江舟山。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to garrison Zhoushan in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon posted to Zhoushan in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 擢四川提督。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Sichuan provincial commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was made provincial commander-in-chief of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 英先以軍功加左都督，授世職拖沙喇哈番。

translations.literal: Ying had earlier been given Left Censor-in-Chief for military merit and granted the hereditary rank of Tuo Shala Ha Fan.
translations.idiomatic: For earlier campaigns he had been named Left Censor-in-Chief and granted the hereditary rank of Tuo Shala Ha Fan.

sentences.zh: 敘平台、澎功，進世職三等阿達哈哈番。

translations.literal: For merit at Taiwan and Penghu, his hereditary rank was advanced to third-class Ada Ha Ha Fan.
translations.idiomatic: The Taiwan and Penghu campaign raised his hereditary rank to third-class Ada Ha Ha Fan.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，調福建陸路提督，改水師。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year he was transferred to Fujian land forces commander-in-chief, then changed to the naval command.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-sixth year he was moved to command Fujian's land forces, then switched to the naval command.

sentences.zh: 上南巡，英朝行在，賜御書榜額。

translations.literal: When the emperor made a southern tour, Ying attended at the traveling palace and was given an imperial inscribed plaque.
translations.idiomatic: On the emperor's southern tour Ying attended the traveling court and received an imperial inscribed plaque.

sentences.zh: 召見，問：「福建今有無海寇？

translations.literal: Summoned to audience, the emperor asked: "Are there sea bandits in Fujian now?"
translations.idiomatic: Called before the throne, he was asked whether Fujian still had sea bandits.

sentences.zh: 」英對曰：「海寇斷不至蔓延，若蔓延，任臣等何用？

translations.literal: Ying answered: "Sea bandits will certainly not spread widely; if they did spread, what use would your servants be?"
translations.idiomatic: Ying replied: "They will never spread in force—if they did, what good are we?"

sentences.zh: 惟海中與城郭不同，一水汪洋，乘一小舟，隨處可藏匿。

translations.literal: Only the sea differs from walled cities: one vast expanse of water—a small boat can hide anywhere.
translations.idiomatic: The sea is not like a walled town: on open water a single small boat can hide almost anywhere.

sentences.zh: 商賈失利，不得已走而為盜，往往有之，不可遽謂之海寇也。

translations.literal: When merchants suffer losses and have no choice but to turn to robbery, this often happens and cannot hastily be called sea banditry."
translations.idiomatic: Merchants who lose their stake sometimes take to piracy—that is common and should not at once be called full-scale sea banditry."

sentences.zh: 」上降詔獎英篤實而明達，尋授威略將軍，仍領水師提督事，复御製詩賜之，勗以黽勉防微。

translations.literal: The emperor issued an edict praising Ying as sincere and clear-sighted, soon appointed him General of Majestic Strategy, still in charge of naval commander-in-chief affairs, again bestowed an imperial poem, and exhorted him to strive diligently and guard against small beginnings.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his plain good sense, named him General of Majestic Strategy while keeping him on the naval command, gave him an imperial poem, and urged steady vigilance against trouble in the bud.

sentences.zh: 五十一年，卒，年七十六，贈太子少保。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year he died at seventy-six and was posthumously given Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifty-first year at seventy-six and was posthumously honored as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: =藍理=藍理，字義山，福建漳浦人。

translations.literal: Lan Li, style name Yishan, was from Zhangpu in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Lan Li, whose style was Yishan, came from Zhangpu in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 少桀驁，膂力絕人。

translations.literal: In youth he was fierce and unruly, with strength beyond ordinary men.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was wild and possessed extraordinary strength.

sentences.zh: 集族人勇健者擊殺海寇盧質，詣吏，欲因以為功，吏疑亦盜也，系之獄。

translations.literal: He gathered stalwart clansmen and killed the sea bandit Lu Zhi, then went to the magistrate hoping to claim merit; the official suspected he was also a bandit and imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: He rallied clansmen, killed the pirate Lu Zhi, and went to the magistrate for credit; the official suspected him of banditry and jailed him.

sentences.zh: 康熙十三年，耿精忠反，悉縱系者，令赴籓下授職。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Kangxi, when Geng Jingzhong rebelled, all prisoners were released and ordered to come to the prince's camp for appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When Geng Jingzhong rebelled in the thirteenth year of Kangxi, prisoners were freed and told to join his service.

sentences.zh: 理間道走仙霞關詣康親王軍降，為鄉導，破叛將曾養性於溫州。

translations.literal: Li went by a secret route through Xianxia Pass to surrender to Prince Kang's army, served as a local guide, and defeated the rebel general Zeng Yangxing at Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li slipped through Xianxia Pass to Prince Kang's camp, guided the army, and helped defeat Zeng Yangxing at Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 十五年，從師入閩，授建寧游擊。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he followed the army into Fujian and was appointed mobile corps commander at Jianning.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he entered Fujian with the army and was made mobile commander at Jianning.

sentences.zh: 十七年，從都統賚塔敗海寇於蜈蚣統賚塔敗海寇於蜈蚣山，复長泰。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, following Commander-in-Chief Baita, he defeated sea bandits at Centipede Mountain and recovered Changtai.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he followed Commander Baita, defeated sea bandits at Centipede Mountain, and retook Changtai.

sentences.zh: 十八年，遷灌口營參將。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was transferred to colonel of Guankou Camp.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was made colonel of Guankou Camp.

sentences.zh: 十九年，總督姚啟聖駐師漳浦，令理分兵守高浦，辭不赴，劾理虛兵冒餉，坐奪官。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year Governor-General Yao Qisheng stationed troops at Zhangpu and ordered Li to divide forces to guard Gaopu; he declined to go; Li was impeached for false rolls and drawing rations, and was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year Yao Qisheng camped at Zhangpu and ordered Li to hold Gaopu; Li refused; he was charged with padding rolls and drawing pay and lost his post.

sentences.zh: 下部議罪，擬杖徒，理請剿海寇自贖，上允之，發軍前效力。

translations.literal: The case was sent down for judgment; beating and penal servitude were proposed; Li asked to suppress sea bandits to redeem himself; the emperor approved and sent him to serve at the front.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Punishments proposed beating and exile; Li asked to fight pirates to atone; the emperor agreed and sent him to the front.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，提督施琅徵台灣，知理英勇，奏署右營游擊領舟師，部議格之，特旨允行。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year Commander-in-Chief Shi Lang campaigned against Taiwan, knowing Li's valor, memorialized appointing him acting Right Camp mobile commander to lead the fleet; the ministry objected, but a special edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year Shi Lang invaded Taiwan, knew Li's courage, and asked to put him in charge of the fleet as acting Right Camp commander; the ministry blocked it, but the emperor overruled them.

sentences.zh: 瑯令理當前鋒，諸弟瑤、瑗、珠皆從。

translations.literal: Lang ordered Li to take the vanguard; his brothers Yao, Yuan, and Zhu all followed.
translations.idiomatic: Lang put Li in the vanguard with his brothers Yao, Yuan, and Zhu beside him.

sentences.zh: 鄭克塽遣其將劉國軒守澎湖，令曾遂等率眾數万迎敵，戰艦蔽海。

translations.literal: Zheng Keshuang sent his general Liu Guoxuan to guard Penghu and ordered Zeng Sui and others to lead tens of thousands to meet the enemy; warships covered the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Keshuang put Liu Guoxuan in Penghu and sent Zeng Sui with tens of thousands to meet the fleet; enemy ships blackened the sea.

sentences.zh: 理督兵與戰，自辰至午，戰益力。

translations.literal: Li directed troops in battle from the hour chen to the hour wu, fighting ever harder.
translations.idiomatic: Li fought from morning to midday, growing fiercer as the battle wore on.

sentences.zh: 遂發砲，彈掠理而過，理僕，遂遙呼曰：「藍理死矣！

translations.literal: Sui fired cannon; a shot grazed Li and he fell; Sui shouted from afar: "Lan Li is dead!"
translations.idiomatic: Sui opened fire; a ball grazed Li and he fell; Sui cried from a distance: "Lan Li is dead!"

sentences.zh: 」瑤扶理起立，理亦呼曰：「藍理在，曾遂死矣！

translations.literal: Yao helped Li stand; Li also shouted: "Lan Li is here—Zeng Sui is the one who will die!"
translations.idiomatic: Yao helped him up; Li shouted back: "Lan Li lives—Zeng Sui will die!"

sentences.zh: 」呼刀，族子法以授理，見理腹破腸流出，為掬而納諸腹，瑗傅以衣，珠持匹練縛其創。

translations.literal: He called for a blade; his clansman Fa handed one to Li; seeing Li's belly torn and intestines spilling out, Fa gathered them and pushed them back in; Yuan bound them with clothing; Zhu held a bolt of silk to tie the wound.
translations.idiomatic: He called for a sword; clansman Fa gave him one; when his belly was torn open Fa pushed his entrails back in, Yuan wrapped him in cloth, and Zhu bound the wound with silk.

sentences.zh: 理呼殺賊，麾兵進，擊沈敵艦二，敵大潰。

translations.literal: Li shouted to kill the enemy, waved the troops forward, sank two enemy vessels, and the foe collapsed in great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Li roared to press the attack, sank two enemy ships, and the enemy broke completely.

sentences.zh: 瑯過理舟慰勞之，令治創复戰。

translations.literal: Lang passed Li's boat to comfort him and ordered his wounds treated so he could fight again.
translations.idiomatic: Lang came alongside to comfort him and told him to dress his wounds and return to battle.

sentences.zh: 瑯舟膠淺沙，敵艦環圍之，理聞，赴援。

translations.literal: Lang's boat grounded on a shoal and enemy vessels surrounded it; when Li heard, he went to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Lang's ship ran aground and enemy vessels closed in; Li hurried to his aid.

sentences.zh: 理舟書姓名篷上，敵憚理，戰為稍卻，追擊，大敗之。

translations.literal: Li had his name written on the sail of his boat; the enemy feared Li, the fighting slackened somewhat, he pursued, and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: His name was painted on his sail; the enemy feared him, gave ground, and he pursued them to a rout.

sentences.zh: 得敵艦，請瑯易舟，出，逐敵至西嶼，殺傷殆盡，遂克澎湖。

translations.literal: Taking an enemy vessel, he asked Lang to change boats, went out, pursued the enemy to Xiyu, killed and wounded nearly all, and thus took Penghu.
translations.idiomatic: He seized an enemy ship, put Lang aboard it, chased the foe to Xiyu, killed or wounded nearly all of them, and Penghu fell.

sentences.zh: 台灣平，敘功，仍授參將，加左都督。

translations.literal: When Taiwan was pacified, merit was recorded; he was again appointed colonel and given Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: After Taiwan was pacified he was again made colonel and named Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 未幾，丁父憂。

translations.literal: Before long he entered mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: He soon went into mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，服闋，詣京師，迎駕趙北口，召至御前，問澎湖戰狀，命解衣視其創，慰勞甚至，超授陝西神木營副將。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, when mourning ended, he went to the capital, met the imperial procession at Zhaobeikou, was summoned before the throne and asked about the Penghu battle, ordered to remove his clothes so his wounds could be seen, comforted with exceptional kindness, and specially promoted to deputy commander of Shenmu Camp in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended in the twenty-sixth year he went to court, met the emperor at Zhaobeikou, was asked about Penghu, made to show his wounds, warmly praised, and abruptly promoted to deputy commander at Shenmu Camp in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 尋擢宣化鎮總兵，掛鎮朔將軍印。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to regional commander of Xuanhua Garrison and given the seal of General Who Guards the North.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made regional commander of Xuanhua with the seal of General Who Guards the North.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，移定海。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was transferred to Dinghai.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he was posted to Dinghai.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，复移天津。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year he was again transferred to Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-second year he was moved again to Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 賜花翎、冠服，並御書榜曰「所向無敵」賚焉。

translations.literal: He was given peacock feathers, court dress, and an imperial inscribed plaque reading "Invincible Wherever He Turns," bestowed together.
translations.idiomatic: He received peacock feathers, court dress, and an imperial plaque inscribed "Invincible Wherever He Turns."

sentences.zh: 四十三年，以舊傷疾作，乞解任，溫旨慰留，遣御醫診視。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year, as old wounds flared, he asked to resign; a gracious edict comforted him and kept him in office, and an imperial physician was sent to examine him.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-third year his old wounds troubled him and he asked to retire; the emperor kindly kept him on and sent a court physician.

sentences.zh: 理以畿輔地多荒窪，請於天津開墾水田百五十頃，歲收稻穀，民號曰「藍田」。

translations.literal: Li, noting that the capital region had much waste lowland, asked to open one hundred fifty qing of paddy at Tianjin; each year rice was harvested and the people called it "Lan's Fields."
translations.idiomatic: Seeing much waste land around the capital, he reclaimed one hundred fifty qing of paddy at Tianjin; the harvest earned the name "Lan's Fields."

sentences.zh: 四十五年，擢福建陸路提督。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year he was promoted to Fujian land forces provincial commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fifth year he was made provincial commander-in-chief of Fujian's land forces.

sentences.zh: 四十六年，上南巡，理迎駕揚州，賞賚有加，复御書榜曰「勇壯簡易」。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year, on the emperor's southern tour, Li met the procession at Yangzhou with added rewards, and again received an imperial plaque reading "Brave, Sturdy, and Plain."
translations.idiomatic: On the southern tour in the forty-sixth year he met the emperor at Yangzhou with extra gifts and a new plaque: "Brave, Sturdy, and Plain."

sentences.zh: 四十七年，丁母憂，命在任守制。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year he entered mourning for his mother and was ordered to observe mourning while remaining in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-seventh year he mourned his mother but was told to remain on duty.

sentences.zh: 五十年，巨盜陳五顯等糾二千人擾泉州永春、德化諸縣。

translations.literal: In the fiftieth year the great bandit Chen Wuxian and others gathered two thousand men to harass Yongchun, Dehua, and other counties in Quanzhou prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fiftieth year the bandit Chen Wuxian rallied two thousand men and raided Yongchun, Dehua, and other Quanzhou counties.

sentences.zh: 事聞逾數月，理始疏陳，並言村落安集如故，上斥其誑，命奪職，總督梁鼐、巡撫滿保先後劾理貪婪酷虐諸狀，遣侍郎和託、廖騰煃會督撫按治得實，論斬，詔從寬免死，入京旗。

translations.literal: The affair was reported only after several months when Li at last memorialized, also saying villages were settled as before; the emperor rebuked his deception, ordered removal from office; Governor-General Liang Nai and Grand Coordinator Manbao successively impeached Li for greed, cruelty, and other charges; Vice Ministers Hetuo and Liao Tengqi were sent with the governor and coordinator to investigate, found the facts true, judged death, but an edict pardoned him from execution and enrolled him in the Beijing Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Months passed before Li reported the outbreak and claimed the countryside was calm; the emperor called it deceit and stripped his office; Liang Nai and Manbao charged him with greed and cruelty; Hetuo and Liao Tengqi confirmed the charges and recommended death, but the emperor spared his life and enrolled him in the Beijing Banner.

sentences.zh: 五十四年，師北征，剿策妄阿喇布坦，理請赴軍前效力，賜總兵銜，從都統穆爾賽協理北路軍務。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fourth year the army marched north against Tsewang Arabtan; Li asked to serve at the front, was given regional commander rank, and followed Commander-in-Chief Muer Sai in managing northern route military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-fourth year, during the northern campaign against Tsewang Arabtan, Li volunteered for the front, was given regional commander rank, and served under Commander-in-Chief Muer Sai on the northern front.

sentences.zh: 以病回京，尋卒。

translations.literal: He returned to the capital because of illness and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: Illness forced him back to the capital, and he died soon after.

sentences.zh: 詔免所追銀兩，遣其妻子回籍歸葬。

translations.literal: An edict remitted the silver he had been ordered to repay and sent his wife and children back to their native place for burial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor canceled the fines levied against him and sent his family home for burial.

sentences.zh: 理虓勇善戰。

translations.literal: Li was fierce, brave, and skilled in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Li was ferocious in battle and fought superbly.

sentences.zh: 性率直。

translations.literal: In disposition he was blunt and straightforward.
translations.idiomatic: He was blunt by nature.

sentences.zh: 官福建提督，政行於鄉里。

translations.literal: As Fujian commander-in-chief, his administration was effective in his home district.
translations.idiomatic: As Fujian commander-in-chief his authority was felt throughout his home country.

sentences.zh: 捕治盜賊，遂及諸豪家。

translations.literal: In capturing and punishing bandits he reached many powerful local families.
translations.idiomatic: His pursuit of bandits eventually touched powerful local clans.

sentences.zh: 修橋樑，平道路，率富民錢，益積怨。

translations.literal: He repaired bridges and leveled roads, levying money from wealthy households, and thus accumulated resentment.
translations.idiomatic: He rebuilt bridges and roads at rich men's expense and bred more resentment.

sentences.zh: 泉州民繪虎為榜，列理諸累民狀，以是得罪。

translations.literal: The people of Quanzhou painted a tiger as a placard and listed Li's acts of harming the people; for this he fell into disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhou townsfolk posted a tiger placard listing his abuses of the people, and that was how he fell afoul of the court.

sentences.zh: 上念其舊功，終矜全之。

translations.literal: The emperor, mindful of his old merit, in the end showed pity and preserved his life.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor remembered his old service and in the end spared him.

sentences.zh: 弟瑤，未仕；

translations.literal: His younger brother Yao did not take office;
translations.idiomatic: His brother Yao never held office;

sentences.zh: 瑗，官至金門總兵；

translations.literal: Yuan rose to Kinmen regional commander;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan rose to regional commander of Kinmen;

sentences.zh: 珠，累官參將。

translations.literal: Zhu rose step by step to colonel.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu eventually became a colonel.

sentences.zh: =黃梧=黃梧，字君宣，福建平和人。

translations.literal: Huang Wu, style name Junxuan, was from Pinghe in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Wu, whose style was Junxuan, came from Pinghe in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 初為鄭成功總兵，守海澄。

translations.literal: At first he was Zheng Chenggong's regional commander, guarding Haicheng.
translations.idiomatic: He had first been Zheng Chenggong's regional commander at Haicheng.

sentences.zh: 順治十三年，梧斬成功將華棟等，以海澄降。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Shunzhi, Wu beheaded Chenggong's generals Hua Dong and others and surrendered Haicheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Shunzhi he killed Chenggong's generals Hua Dong and others and surrendered Haicheng.

sentences.zh: 大將軍鄭親王世子濟度以聞，封海澄公。

translations.literal: Grand General Prince of Zheng's heir Jidu reported it, and he was enfeoffed as Duke of Haicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Prince of Zheng's heir Jidu reported the surrender and Wu was enfeoffed as Duke of Haicheng.

sentences.zh: 十四年，總督李率泰疏請益梧兵，合四千人，駐漳州。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, Governor-General Li Shuätai memorialized requesting additional troops for Wu, totaling four thousand men, stationed at Zhangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, Governor-General Li Shuätai asked the throne for more troops under Wu—four thousand in all—to garrison Zhangzhou.

sentences.zh: 梧與李率泰及提督馬得功、都統郎賽水陸分道進，破七城，克閩安鎮。

translations.literal: Wu together with Li Shuätai, provincial commander-in-chief Ma Degong, and commander Lang Sai advanced by separate land and sea routes, captured seven cities, and took Min'an Fort.
translations.idiomatic: Wu, Li Shuätai, provincial commander Ma Degong, and Banner commander Lang Sai advanced on separate land and sea routes, took seven cities, and captured Min'an Fort.

sentences.zh: 敘功，賜甲胄、貂裘，加太子太保。

translations.literal: When merits were recorded, he was granted armor and a sable fur coat and advanced to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he received armor and a sable coat and was promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 梧牒李率泰，薦委署都督施琅智勇忠誠，熟諳沿海事狀，假以事權，必能剪除海孽；

translations.literal: Wu wrote to Li Shuätai recommending acting regional commander Shi Lang as intelligent, brave, loyal, and sincere, thoroughly familiar with coastal conditions; if entrusted with authority, he would surely be able to exterminate the maritime rebels;
translations.idiomatic: Wu wrote Li Shuätai urging that acting regional commander Shi Lang—intelligent, brave, loyal, and well versed in coastal affairs—be given real authority; with it, Wu argued, he could wipe out the sea rebels.

sentences.zh: 又言成功全藉內地接濟，木植、絲綿、油麻、釘鐵、柴米，土宄陰為轉輸，齎糧養寇，請嚴禁；

translations.literal: He also said that Chenggong wholly relied on supplies from the interior—timber, silk and cotton, hemp oil, nails and iron, firewood and rice—with local ruffians secretly transporting them to feed the rebels, and requested strict prohibition;
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that Chenggong depended entirely on inland supplies—timber, silk, cotton, hemp oil, nails, iron, firewood, and rice—and that local bandits were secretly moving goods to sustain the enemy; he asked that this be strictly forbidden.

sentences.zh: 併條列滅賊五策，復請速誅成功父芝龍。

translations.literal: He further set forth in detail five strategies for destroying the bandits and again requested the speedy execution of Chenggong's father Zhilong.
translations.idiomatic: He also laid out five detailed plans for destroying the rebels and again urged the immediate execution of Chenggong's father, Zhilong.

sentences.zh: 率泰先後上聞，瑯得擢用，芝龍亦誅。

translations.literal: Shuätai reported these matters in succession to the throne; Lang was promoted and employed, and Zhilong was also executed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shuätai forwarded these recommendations in turn; Shi Lang was promoted and put to use, and Zhilong was executed.

sentences.zh: 尋命嚴海禁，絕接濟，移兵分駐海濱，阻成功兵登岸，增戰艦，習水戰，皆用梧議也。

translations.literal: Soon orders were issued to tighten the maritime ban, cut off supplies, relocate troops to garrison the seacoast in detachments, block Chenggong's troops from landing, increase warships, and drill in naval warfare—all adopting Wu's proposals.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the court tightened the maritime ban, cut off supplies, redeployed troops along the coast, blocked Chenggong's men from landing, added warships, and trained for naval combat—all following Wu's advice.

sentences.zh: 及成功病卒，其將萬義、萬祿、楊學皋、陳莽、陳輝、顏立勳、黃昌、黃義、餘期英等詣梧降。

translations.literal: When Chenggong died of illness, his generals Wan Yi, Wan Lu, Yang Xuegao, Chen Mang, Chen Hui, Yan Lixun, Huang Chang, Huang Yi, Yu Qiying, and others came to Wu to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: After Chenggong died of illness, his generals Wan Yi, Wan Lu, Yang Xuegao, Chen Mang, Chen Hui, Yan Lixun, Huang Chang, Huang Yi, Yu Qiying, and others came to Wu and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 康熙二年，師攻廈門，靖南王耿繼茂出潯尾，梧偕李率泰出蒿嶼，督水陸將卒夾擊，斬獲無算，遂克廈門、金門、浯嶼三島。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kangxi, the army attacked Xiamen; Prince of Jingnan Geng Jimao sortied from Xunwei, Wu together with Li Shuätai sortied from Haoyu, and they directed land and naval officers and men in a pincer attack, slaying and capturing beyond count, and thus took the three islands of Xiamen, Kinmen, and Wuyu.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kangxi the army attacked Xiamen. Prince of Jingnan Geng Jimao moved out from Xunwei while Wu and Li Shuätai sortied from Haoyu; directing land and sea forces in a pincer, they killed and captured beyond count and took Xiamen, Kinmen, and Wuyu.

sentences.zh: 鄭錦遁據銅山。

translations.literal: Zheng Jing fled and occupied Tongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Jing withdrew and held Tongshan.

sentences.zh: 繼茂令梧統兵駐雲霄防剿。

translations.literal: Jimao ordered Wu to command troops garrisoned at Yunxiao for defense and suppression.
translations.idiomatic: Jimao ordered Wu to take command of troops garrisoned at Yunxiao to defend and suppress the enemy.

sentences.zh: 三年，梧招錦將周全斌、陳昇、黃廷、何政、許貞、李思忠等來降。

translations.literal: In the third year, Wu induced Zheng Jing's generals Zhou Quanbin, Chen Sheng, Huang Ting, He Zheng, Xu Zhen, Li Sizhong, and others to come and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Wu persuaded Zheng Jing's generals Zhou Quanbin, Chen Sheng, Huang Ting, He Zheng, Xu Zhen, Li Sizhong, and others to defect.

sentences.zh: 遂偕繼茂、李率泰及提督王進功乘夜渡海，拔銅山。

translations.literal: He then together with Jimao, Li Shuätai, and provincial commander-in-chief Wang Jingong crossed the sea by night and captured Tongshan.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Jimao, Li Shuätai, and provincial commander Wang Jingong in a night crossing and captured Tongshan.

sentences.zh: 錦走還台灣。

translations.literal: Jing fled back to Taiwan.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Jing fled back to Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 梧疏言：「自海上歸誠，十二年中，先後招撫文武吏二百餘、兵數万人，有蒙賜封侯伯且世襲者。

translations.literal: Wu memorialized: "Since submitting from the sea, over twelve years I have successively induced civil and military officials numbering more than two hundred and troops numbering tens of thousands to submit, some having received enfeoffment as marquis or earl with hereditary succession."
translations.idiomatic: Wu memorialized: "In the twelve years since I came in from the sea, I have successively induced more than two hundred civil and military officers and tens of thousands of troops to submit—some of whom were enfeoffed as marquis or earl with hereditary succession."

sentences.zh: 臣公爵未定何等及承襲次數，乞敕部覈議。

translations.literal: My ducal rank has not been fixed as to grade or number of inheritances; I beg that the ministry be ordered to examine and deliberate."
translations.idiomatic: My own ducal rank has not been fixed in grade or in the number of inheritances; I ask that the ministry be ordered to review the matter."

sentences.zh: 」尋命定封一等公，世襲十二次。

translations.literal: " Soon an order fixed his enfeoffment as a first-rank duke with twelve generations of hereditary succession.
translations.idiomatic: " The court soon fixed his title as a first-class duke, inheritable for twelve generations.

sentences.zh: 七年，兵部議裁汰諸行省兵額，梧標下額定官三十員、兵一千二百人，餘移駐河南。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, the Board of War deliberated cutting army quotas in the various provinces; under Wu's banner the fixed quota was thirty officers and twelve hundred soldiers, with the remainder transferred to garrison Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the Board of War proposed cutting provincial troop quotas; Wu's command was fixed at thirty officers and twelve hundred men, with the rest transferred to garrison Henan.

sentences.zh: 十三年，耿精忠反，傳檄至漳州。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Geng Jingzhong rebelled and his proclamation reached Zhangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Geng Jingzhong rebelled and his manifesto reached Zhangzhou.

sentences.zh: 梧方病疽，聞變驚恚，遂卒。

translations.literal: Wu was then ill with carbuncle; hearing of the uprising he was alarmed and enraged, and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: Wu was then ill with a carbuncle; shocked and enraged by the rebellion, he soon died.

sentences.zh: 子芳度，字壽岩。

translations.literal: His son Fangdu, style name Shouyan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fangdu, courtesy name Shouyan.

sentences.zh: 梧既卒，陽以梧命答精忠，而陰募兵自守，凡二月餘，得壯士六千人，遂斬精忠所置都督劉豹等，誓師登陴，以蠟丸函疏，遣黃藍間道馳奏。

translations.literal: After Wu died, Fangdu outwardly answered Jingzhong in Wu's name but secretly recruited troops to defend himself; in a little over two months he obtained six thousand stalwart men, then beheaded regional commanders Liu Bao and others appointed by Jingzhong, swore his forces and mounted the ramparts, and sent a memorial sealed in a wax pill by Huang Lan by a secret route at full speed to report to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu died, Fangdu outwardly replied to Jingzhong in his father's name while secretly raising troops to defend the city. In little more than two months he gathered six thousand stalwarts, beheaded regional commanders Liu Bao and others appointed by Jingzhong, rallied his men on the walls, and sent Huang Lan by a secret route with a wax-sealed memorial to the throne.

sentences.zh: 上嘉梧忠藎，降詔優恤，以芳度襲爵；

translations.literal: The emperor praised Wu's loyalty and devotion and issued an edict of generous condolence, having Fangdu inherit the title;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised Wu's loyalty and issued a generous edict of condolence, allowing Fangdu to inherit the title;

sentences.zh: 並諭師自浙江、江西、廣東三路入福建。

translations.literal: and also ordered the armies to enter Fujian by three routes from Zhejiang, Jiangxi, and Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: and ordered imperial forces to enter Fujian from Zhejiang, Jiangxi, and Guangdong in three columns.

sentences.zh: 芳度诇何路兵先到，迎會合剿。

translations.literal: Fangdu reconnoitered which route's troops would arrive first and went to meet and join in combined suppression.
translations.idiomatic: Fangdu scouted which column would arrive first and went out to meet it for a joint campaign.

sentences.zh: 尋疏言：「漳州介耿、鄭二逆間，自八月以來，堅與耿拒，偽與鄭和。

translations.literal: Soon he memorialized: "Zhangzhou lies between the two rebels Geng and Zheng; since the eighth month I have firmly resisted Geng while feigning reconciliation with Zheng."
translations.idiomatic: He soon memorialized: "Zhangzhou sits between the Geng and Zheng rebels. Since the eighth month I have held firm against Geng while pretending to reconcile with Zheng."

sentences.zh: 因得陰行招募，練成勁旅萬人，分佈漳城及龍溪等五縣。

translations.literal: Thus I have been able secretly to recruit men and drill a crack force of ten thousand, distributed through Zhangzhou city and five counties including Longxi."
translations.idiomatic: That let me recruit in secret and train a crack force of ten thousand men, posted across Zhangzhou city and five counties including Longxi."

sentences.zh: 無何，耿逆來犯，臣率眾迎擊，擒斬無算。

translations.literal: Before long the Geng rebel came to attack; I led the masses to meet the assault and captured and beheaded beyond count."
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Geng rebels attacked; I led my men out to meet them and killed and captured beyond count."

sentences.zh: 二逆構怨已深，勢必俱敗。

translations.literal: The two rebels' enmity is already deep; they are bound to fail together."
translations.idiomatic: Bad blood between the two rebels already runs deep; they are bound to destroy each other."

sentences.zh: 誠得粵省大兵乘勝進攻，臣當率師迎會，迅奏掃除之功。

translations.literal: If indeed Guangdong's great army can follow up victory with an attack, I shall lead my forces to meet and join, swiftly reporting the achievement of complete pacification."
translations.idiomatic: If Guangdong's main force presses the attack while victory is at hand, I will lead my troops out to join it and quickly report the work of total pacification."

sentences.zh: 」十四年，復言：「臣拒耿餌鄭，固守一載有餘。

translations.literal: " In the fourteenth year he again said: "I have resisted Geng while baiting Zheng, holding firm for more than a year."
translations.idiomatic: " In the fourteenth year he wrote again: "I have resisted Geng while stringing Zheng along, holding the city for more than a year."

sentences.zh: 近二逆通好，​​臣謀已洩。

translations.literal: Recently the two rebels have made peace; my plot has been exposed."
translations.idiomatic: Recently the two rebels made peace, and my stratagem was exposed."

sentences.zh: 鄭逆遂撤回各鎮，蜂聚海澄，備糧繕器。

translations.literal: The Zheng rebel then withdrew from the various garrisons and swarmed together at Haicheng, storing grain and repairing weapons."
translations.idiomatic: The Zheng rebels then pulled back from their garrisons, massed at Haicheng, and began stockpiling grain and repairing arms."

sentences.zh: 臣知其狡謀，遣總兵楊壯猷等扼守平和，並令臣從兄芳泰突圍赴廣東，接引大兵。

translations.literal: Knowing his cunning plan, I sent regional commander Yang Zhuangyou and others to hold Pinghe, and also ordered my elder cousin Fangtai to break out and go to Guangdong to guide the great army."
