translations.idiomatic: Seeing through his scheme, I sent regional commander Yang Zhuangyou and others to hold Pinghe and ordered my elder cousin Fangtai to break out toward Guangdong and guide the main force."

sentences.zh: 鄭逆率眾圍城，晝夜攻擊。

translations.literal: The Zheng rebel led his masses to besiege the city, attacking day and night."
translations.idiomatic: The Zheng rebels besieged the city and attacked day and night."

sentences.zh: 臣連次出兵，斬其將黃鼎新、盧英等。

translations.literal: I repeatedly sortied and beheaded his generals Huang Dingxin, Lu Ying, and others."
translations.idiomatic: I sortied again and again and killed his generals Huang Dingxin, Lu Ying, and others."

sentences.zh: 但孤城缺餉，百計難支。

translations.literal: But the isolated city lacks provisions; by every stratagem it is hard to hold."
translations.idiomatic: But an isolated city short of supplies cannot be held by any stratagem."

sentences.zh: 計粵路援師，旦夕可至。

translations.literal: I reckon that relief from the Guangdong route can arrive within a day or two."
translations.idiomatic: I expect relief from Guangdong to arrive within a day or two."

sentences.zh: 乞密敕浙江、江西兩路兵迅速進發，俾二逆不能相顧，臣可會合奏功。

translations.literal: I beg a secret edict for the armies of the Zhejiang and Jiangxi routes to advance swiftly, so that the two rebels cannot look to each other and I can join forces and report success."
translations.idiomatic: I beg a secret order for the Zhejiang and Jiangxi columns to advance at once, so the two rebels cannot aid each other and I can join up and report success."

sentences.zh: 漳州自五月被圍至七月，敵來益眾，豎雲梯攻城，砲毀城堞三十餘丈。

translations.literal: From the fifth month when Zhangzhou was besieged until the seventh month, the enemy came in ever greater numbers, erected cloud ladders to assault the city, and cannon fire destroyed more than thirty zhang of the parapet.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangzhou was under siege from the fifth month through the seventh; the enemy grew ever stronger, raised siege ladders, and cannon fire smashed more than thirty zhang of the battlements.

sentences.zh: 芳度率將士拒戰，殲賊無算。

translations.literal: Fangdu led officers and men in resisting battle and destroyed bandits beyond count.
translations.idiomatic: Fangdu led his officers and men in defense and killed rebels beyond count.

sentences.zh: 敵環攻不退，芳度連疏告急。

translations.literal: The enemy surrounded and attacked without retreating; Fangdu repeatedly memorialized in urgent appeal.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy kept up the encirclement; Fangdu sent memorial after memorial begging for relief.

sentences.zh: 詔趣統兵諸將迅速赴援，並撥餉接濟。

translations.literal: An edict urged the various generals commanding troops to hasten to relief and also allocated funds for supply.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the commanding generals to hurry to the rescue and allocated funds for relief supplies.

sentences.zh: 十月，城中糧盡，叛將吳淑引賊陷城。

translations.literal: In the tenth month provisions in the city were exhausted; the turncoat general Wu Shu led bandits to take the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the city ran out of grain; the turncoat Wu Shu led the enemy inside and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 芳度率兵巷戰，力竭，赴開元寺井死，年二十有五。

translations.literal: Fangdu led troops in street fighting until strength was spent, then went to Kaiyuan Temple's well and died, aged twenty-five.
translations.idiomatic: Fangdu fought house to house until he was spent, then drowned himself in the well at Kaiyuan Temple. He was twenty-five.

sentences.zh: 賊戕其屍，母趙、妻李自經。

translations.literal: The bandits mutilated his corpse; his mother Zhao and wife Li hanged themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels mutilated his body; his mother Zhao and his wife Li hanged themselves.

sentences.zh: 從父樞、從兄芳名、弟芳聲、芳祐並死。

translations.literal: His uncle Shu, elder cousin Fangming, younger brothers Fang Sheng and Fang You all died together.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Shu, elder cousin Fangming, and younger brothers Fang Sheng and Fang You all died with him.

sentences.zh: 期功男女從死者三十餘人。

translations.literal: More than thirty men and women of near kin died following him.
translations.idiomatic: More than thirty close relatives, men and women, died with him.

sentences.zh: 賊又斫梧棺，毀其屍。

translations.literal: The bandits also hacked open Wu's coffin and destroyed his corpse.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels also broke open Wu's coffin and desecrated his remains.

sentences.zh: 副將蔡隆，游擊硃武，外委張瓊、戴鄰、陳謙俱罵賊死。

translations.literal: Vice commander Cai Long, battalion commander Zhu Wu, and staff officers Zhang Qiong, Dai Lin, and Chen Qian all cursed the bandits and died.
translations.idiomatic: Vice commander Cai Long, battalion commander Zhu Wu, and staff officers Zhang Qiong, Dai Lin, and Chen Qian all died cursing the enemy.

sentences.zh: 事聞，優詔褒卹，贈芳度王爵，諡忠勇，如多羅郡王例，遣大臣致祭。

translations.literal: When the affair was reported, a generous edict of praise and condolence was issued; Fangdu was posthumously granted princely rank, given the posthumous title Zhongyong, with rites like those for a Prince of the Multitude, and a minister was sent to perform sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the throne, an edict praised and mourned him: Fangdu was posthumously made a prince with the temple name Loyal and Brave, given rites on the model of a Prince of the Multitude, and a minister was sent to offer sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 隆、武、瓊、鄰、謙俱贈官有差。

translations.literal: Long, Wu, Qiong, Lin, and Qian were all posthumously granted office with varying ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Long, Wu, Qiong, Lin, and Qian were all posthumously given offices of varying rank.

sentences.zh: 梧兄子芳世，字周士。

translations.literal: Wu's brother's son Fangshi, style name Zhoushi.
translations.idiomatic: Wu's nephew Fangshi, courtesy name Zhoushi.

sentences.zh: 先於康熙元年齎梧疏入覲，留京師，授一等侍衛。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the first year of Kangxi, he carried Wu's memorial to the capital for audience and remained in the capital, appointed first-class guard.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the first year of Kangxi, he brought Wu's memorial to court, stayed in the capital, and was appointed a first-class imperial guard.

sentences.zh: 及芳度遣藍齎疏告急，芳世自陳乞從大軍自廣東進援，上許之，以為福建隨徵總兵官，降敕褒勉。

translations.literal: When Fangdu sent Lan bearing a memorial in urgent appeal, Fangshi himself submitted a request to follow the great army advancing in relief from Guangdong; the emperor granted it, appointing him Fujian campaign regional commander, with an edict of praise and encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: When Fangdu sent Lan with an urgent memorial, Fangshi asked to join the relief force coming from Guangdong; the emperor agreed, made him Fujian campaign regional commander, and issued an edict of praise.

sentences.zh: 芳世至廣東，會弟芳泰自漳州突圍出，芳世督兵赴援，距漳州僅二日，聞城陷，退屯惠州。

translations.literal: Fangshi reached Guangdong and met his younger brother Fangtai who had broken out from Zhangzhou; Fangshi directed troops to hurry to relief, only two days from Zhangzhou when he heard the city had fallen, and withdrew to camp at Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fangshi reached Guangdong and met his brother Fangtai, who had broken out of Zhangzhou. He hurried toward the city but was still two days away when he heard it had fallen; he withdrew to camp at Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 芳度殉難，詔以芳世襲爵。

translations.literal: When Fangdu died martyrdom, an edict had Fangshi inherit the title.
translations.idiomatic: After Fangdu's death in battle, an edict had Fangshi inherit the title.

sentences.zh: 十五年，叛將馬雄等誘芳世兄弟附三桂，不從，乘間脫走，至江西信豐，遣藍齎疏陳陷賊始末。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, the turncoat generals Ma Xiong and others tried to induce Fangshi and his brothers to join Wu Sangui; they refused, slipped away at an opportunity, reached Xinfeng in Jiangxi, and sent Lan bearing a memorial detailing how they had fallen among the bandits from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year the turncoat Ma Xiong and others tried to win Fangshi and his brothers to Wu Sangui's side; they refused, slipped away at the first chance, reached Xinfeng in Jiangxi, and sent Lan with a memorial explaining how they had fallen in with the rebels.

sentences.zh: 上嘉之，加太子太保，命仍鎮守漳州。

translations.literal: The emperor praised this, added Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and ordered him still to garrison Zhangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him, added the title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and ordered him to continue garrisoning Zhangzhou.

sentences.zh: 藍自參將擢海澄總兵，令馳赴康親王軍，俟漳、泉恢復，收集海澄公部下散失官兵，鎮守汛地。

translations.literal: Lan was promoted from colonel to Haicheng regional commander and ordered to ride at full speed to Prince Kang's army; when Zhangzhou and Quanzhou were recovered, he was to gather the scattered officers and men of the Duke of Haicheng's command and garrison the posts.
translations.idiomatic: Lan was promoted from colonel to Haicheng regional commander and ordered to ride to Prince Kang's army; once Zhangzhou and Quanzhou were recovered, he was to gather the Duke of Haicheng's scattered officers and men and garrison the posts.

sentences.zh: 十六年，芳世疏言：「臣叔梧遺骸遭賊殘毀，請與芳度一體議卹。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, Fangshi memorialized: "My uncle Wu's remains were mutilated and destroyed by bandits; I request that condolence be deliberated together with Fangdu."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year Fangshi memorialized: "My uncle Wu's remains were mutilated by the rebels; I ask that he receive the same posthumous honors as Fangdu."

sentences.zh: 臣叔樞{罒馬}賊而死，臣弟芳名、芳聲奮力守城，同日遇害，並乞賜卹。

translations.literal: My uncle Shu died reviling the bandits; my younger brothers Fangming and Fang Sheng fought hard defending the city and were killed on the same day; I also beg posthumous grants of condolence."
translations.idiomatic: My uncle Shu died cursing the rebels; my brothers Fangming and Fang Sheng fought to hold the walls and were killed the same day; I ask posthumous honors for them as well."

sentences.zh: 」詔贈梧太保，諡忠恪，樞贈按察使僉事，芳名、芳聲贈太常寺卿，各予廕；

translations.literal: " An edict posthumously granted Wu Grand Guardian, posthumous title Zhongke; Shu was posthumously granted Vice Commissioner of the Surveillance Commission; Fangming and Fang Sheng were posthumously granted Vice Ministers of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, each granted hereditary privilege;
translations.idiomatic: " An edict posthumously made Wu Grand Guardian with the temple name Loyal and Reverent; Shu was made Vice Commissioner of the Surveillance Commission; Fangming and Fang Sheng were made Vice Ministers of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, each with hereditary privilege;

sentences.zh: 賜芳世蟒袍、弓矢、鞍馬，褒嘉甚至。

translations.literal: Fangshi was granted a python robe, bow and arrows, and saddle and horse—the praise and favor were very great.
translations.idiomatic: Fangshi received a python robe, bow and arrows, and saddle and horse—the honors were extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 十七年，錦將劉國軒、吳淑犯海澄，芳世與總督郎廷相、副都統孟安等迭敗之觀音山、秬山頭、石瑪村等處。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, Jing's generals Liu Guoxuan and Wu Shu invaded Haicheng; Fangshi together with Governor-General Lang Tingxiang, vice commander of the Banner Meng An, and others repeatedly defeated them at Guanyin Mountain, Jushantou, Shima Village, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Zheng Jing's generals Liu Guoxuan and Wu Shu attacked Haicheng; Fangshi, Governor-General Lang Tingxiang, Banner vice commander Meng An, and others repeatedly defeated them at Guanyin Mountain, Jushantou, Shima Village, and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 國軒退犯漳州，芳世率兵堵剿，殲賊甚眾。

translations.literal: Guoxuan withdrew and invaded Zhangzhou; Fangshi led troops to block and suppress, destroying very many bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Guoxuan withdrew and turned on Zhangzhou; Fangshi led troops to intercept him and killed a great many rebels.

sentences.zh: 山寇蔡寅詐稱硃三太子，糾眾數万，與錦通，犯漳州。

translations.literal: The mountain bandit Cai Yin falsely claimed to be the Third Prince Zhu, gathered masses numbering tens of thousands, communicated with Jing, and invaded Zhangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The mountain rebel Cai Yin falsely claimed to be the Third Prince Zhu, raised tens of thousands of men, coordinated with Zheng Jing, and attacked Zhangzhou.

sentences.zh: 芳世擊敗之於天寶山，斬其渠楊寧等。

translations.literal: Fangshi defeated him at Tianbao Mountain and beheaded their leader Yang Ning and others.
translations.idiomatic: Fangshi routed him on Tianbao Mountain and beheaded the ringleader Yang Ning and others.

sentences.zh: 芳世疏言：「漳州亂後，臣叔梧、弟芳度舊部離散，臣漸次收集，得四千八百人，選補本標五營六百人，餘無額可補，乞汰留三千人，別立三營，視經制給餉。

translations.literal: Fangshi memorialized: "After the chaos in Zhangzhou, the old subordinates of my uncle Wu and younger brother Fangdu scattered; I have gradually gathered them and obtained forty-eight hundred men, selected six hundred to fill the five battalions of my personal standard, with the remainder having no quota to fill; I beg to retain three thousand after reduction, establish three separate battalions, and pay rations according to the regular establishment."
translations.idiomatic: Fangshi memorialized: "After Zhangzhou's chaos the old followers of my uncle Wu and brother Fangdu scattered. I have gradually reassembled forty-eight hundred men, filled six hundred posts in my five standard battalions, and have no quota for the rest. I ask to keep three thousand after reduction, form three new battalions, and pay them on the regular establishment."

sentences.zh: 」部議從之。

translations.literal: " The ministry deliberated and agreed.
translations.idiomatic: " The Board approved the request.

sentences.zh: 未幾，病卒，遺疏言：「閩省久困兵禍，漳州尤甚。

translations.literal: Before long he died of illness; his final memorial said: "Fujian province has long been afflicted by military calamity, and Zhangzhou especially so."
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died of illness. His final memorial said: "Fujian has long suffered from war, and Zhangzhou worst of all."

sentences.zh: 原大師底定後，嚴飭有司輕徭薄賦，甦此殘黎。

translations.literal: I pray that after the great army pacifies the region, officials be strictly charged to lighten corvée and reduce levies and revive these battered people."
translations.idiomatic: I pray that once the great army has pacified the province, officials will be strictly ordered to lighten labor service and reduce taxes and revive these battered people."

sentences.zh: 」並區畫海疆數事，復以子溥年才九歲，請以弟芳泰襲爵，詔贈少保，諡忠襄。

translations.literal: " He also outlined several matters concerning the maritime frontier, and again because his son Pu was only nine years old requested that his younger brother Fangtai inherit the title; an edict posthumously granted Junior Guardian and posthumous title Zhongxiang.
translations.idiomatic: " He also laid out several plans for the coastal frontier and, because his son Pu was only nine, asked that his brother Fangtai inherit the title. An edict posthumously made him Junior Guardian with the temple name Loyal and Auspicious.

sentences.zh: =芳泰=芳泰，字和士。

translations.literal: Fangtai, style name Heshi.
translations.idiomatic: Fangtai, courtesy name Heshi.

sentences.zh: 少為諸生。

translations.literal: In youth he was a student.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he was a licentiate.

sentences.zh: 佐芳度守漳州，突圍出乞援。

translations.literal: He assisted Fangdu in defending Zhangzhou, broke out and went to beg relief.
translations.idiomatic: He helped Fangdu defend Zhangzhou, broke out of the city, and went to seek relief.

sentences.zh: 城陷後，父母妻子皆遇害。

translations.literal: After the city fell, his parents, wife, and children were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: After the city fell, his parents, wife, and children were all killed.

sentences.zh: 至廣東，值尚之信叛，芳泰與芳世從巡撫楊熙力戰得出。

translations.literal: Reaching Guangdong, he encountered Shang Zhixin's rebellion; Fangtai and Fangshi followed Grand Coordinator Yang Xi and fought hard to get out.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangdong he ran into Shang Zhixin's rebellion; Fangtai and Fangshi fought under Grand Coordinator Yang Xi and battled their way out.

sentences.zh: 尋授江南京口總兵。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Nanjing Jiangkou regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed regional commander at Jiangkou in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 芳世卒，襲爵。

translations.literal: When Fangshi died, he inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: When Fangshi died, he inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 屢出勦賊，復平和、漳平諸縣。

translations.literal: He repeatedly sortied to suppress bandits and recovered Pinghe, Zhangping, and other counties.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly campaigned against bandits and recovered Pinghe, Zhangping, and other counties.

sentences.zh: 總督姚啟聖疏言芳泰年少，不能轄標兵。

translations.literal: Governor-General Yao Qishi memorialized that Fangtai was young and could not command his standard troops.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Yao Qishi reported that Fangtai was too young to command his personal troops.

sentences.zh: 下部議，令芳泰詣京師。

translations.literal: The matter was sent to the ministry for deliberation; Fangtai was ordered to proceed to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The matter went to the ministry, and Fangtai was ordered to come to the capital.

sentences.zh: 芳泰疏請暫駐汀州，為兄芳度營葬。

translations.literal: Fangtai memorialized requesting temporary garrison at Tingzhou to arrange burial for his elder brother Fangdu.
translations.idiomatic: Fangtai asked to stay temporarily at Tingzhou to arrange his brother Fangdu's burial.

sentences.zh: 啟聖復言海澄公標下舊兵，聞芳泰在汀州，皆走依之，偽將吳淑兄弟以曾害芳度，不敢來降，請敕芳泰速離福建。

translations.literal: Qishi again reported that the old troops under the Duke of Haicheng's banner, hearing Fangtai was at Tingzhou, all fled to join him; the false generals Wu Shu and his brothers, because they had once harmed Fangdu, dared not come to surrender, and requested an edict that Fangtai speedily leave Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Qishi added that the Duke of Haicheng's old soldiers, hearing Fangtai was at Tingzhou, were flocking to him; the rebel Wu Shu and his brothers, who had once betrayed Fangdu, dared not surrender while Fangtai remained, and he asked that Fangtai be ordered to leave Fujian at once.

sentences.zh: 十八年，芳泰至京師，上言：「臣久經行陣，不為幼弱。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, Fangtai reached the capital and addressed the throne: "I have long been through campaigns and am not weak from youth."
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year Fangtai reached the capital and said: "I have long seen battle and am no callow youth."

sentences.zh: 離漳已十月，不聞吳淑投誠。

translations.literal: I have been away from Zhangzhou for ten months and have not heard that Wu Shu has submitted."
translations.idiomatic: I have been away from Zhangzhou ten months, and Wu Shu still has not surrendered."

sentences.zh: 督臣無計辦賊，以臣藉口。

translations.literal: The governor has no plan to deal with the bandits and uses me as a pretext."
translations.idiomatic: The governor has no plan for the rebels and is using me as an excuse."

sentences.zh: 臣當壯年，乞仍駐閩疆督剿，以報主恩。

translations.literal: I am still in my prime; I beg still to garrison the Fujian frontier and direct suppression, to repay my lord's grace."
translations.idiomatic: I am still in my prime; I beg to be allowed to remain on the Fujian frontier and lead the campaign, to repay my sovereign's grace."

sentences.zh: 」上慰諭之。

translations.literal: " The emperor comforted and instructed him.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor comforted and reassured him.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，許其回籍營葬。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, he was permitted to return to his native place to arrange burial.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he was allowed to return home to arrange the burial.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，卒，以子應纘為芳度後，襲爵。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he died; his son Yingzuan was made Fangdu's heir and inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he died; his son Yingzuan was made Fangdu's heir and inherited the dukedom.

sentences.zh: 四十九年，應纘為芳泰請卹，贈太子少保。

translations.literal: In the forty-ninth year, Yingzuan requested posthumous honors for Fangtai; he was posthumously granted Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-ninth year Yingzuan petitioned for posthumous honors for Fangtai, who was granted Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，追諡襄愍。

translations.literal: In the early Qianlong reign, the posthumous title Xiangmin was conferred retrospectively.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianlong reign he was posthumously given the temple name Auspicious and Resolute.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，高宗特詔以公爵世襲罔替。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year, the Gaozong Emperor specially issued an edict that the ducal title be inherited in perpetuity.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year the Gaozong Emperor issued a special edict making the dukedom perpetually inheritable.

sentences.zh: 應纘卒，諡溫簡。

translations.literal: When Yingzuan died, his posthumous title was Wenjian.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingzuan died, he was given the temple name Gentle and Simple.

sentences.zh: 無子，以從子仕簡為後，襲爵。

translations.literal: Having no son, a younger cousin Shijian was made his heir and inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: He had no son; a younger cousin, Shijian, was made his heir and inherited the dukedom.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，朝京師。

translations.literal: In the early Qianlong reign, he attended court at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianlong reign he came to court in the capital.

sentences.zh: 高宗以其幼，令還裡待命。

translations.literal: The Gaozong Emperor, because he was young, ordered him to return to his native place and await appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Because he was still young, the Gaozong Emperor sent him home to await further orders.

sentences.zh: 十九年，授衢州總兵。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was appointed regional commander of Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he was made regional commander at Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，遷湖廣提督，歷廣東、福建陸路水師。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was transferred to Huguang provincial commander-in-chief and successively held the land and naval commands of Guangdong and Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he became Huguang provincial commander-in-chief and later served as commander of Guangdong and of Fujian's land and naval forces.

sentences.zh: 疏發廈門商船陋規，上嘉之，諭：「汝知恩，朕亦知人。

translations.literal: He memorialized exposing corrupt customs regarding Xiamen merchant shipping; the emperor praised this and instructed: "You know gratitude; I also know men."
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized exposing abusive fees on Xiamen merchant shipping; the emperor praised him and said: "You know how to repay favor—and I know how to judge men."

sentences.zh: 」漳、泉民流入台灣，屢出劫掠，仕簡親渡海督兵捕治。

translations.literal: " People from Zhangzhou and Quanzhou flowed into Taiwan and repeatedly came out to raid and plunder; Shirjian personally crossed the sea to direct troops in capture and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: " When people from Zhangzhou and Quanzhou drifted to Taiwan and repeatedly raided the coast, Shirjian crossed the strait himself to lead troops against them.

sentences.zh: 再入覲，賜黃馬褂、雙眼花翎、黑狐端罩。

translations.literal: On a second audience at court he was granted a yellow riding jacket, double-eyed peacock feathers, and a black-fox formal surcoat.
translations.idiomatic: On a later visit to court he received a yellow riding jacket, double-eyed peacock feathers, and a black-fox court surcoat.

sentences.zh: 病後偶躓，賜人參、高麗清心丸。

translations.literal: After illness he once stumbled; he was granted ginseng and Korean Heart-Clearing Pills.
translations.idiomatic: After an illness he had a fall, and the emperor sent him ginseng and Korean restorative pills.

sentences.zh: 淡水生番戕同知楊凱，复渡海督兵捕治，加太子太保。

translations.literal: Aboriginal tribesmen of Tamsui killed Subprefect Yang Kai; he again crossed the sea to direct troops in capture and punishment and was advanced to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When aboriginal people in Tamsui killed Subprefect Yang Kai, he crossed the sea again to lead a punitive campaign and was promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 林爽文亂起，督兵討之，師久無功。

translations.literal: When Lin Shuangwen's rebellion broke out, he directed troops to suppress it, but the army long achieved no success.
translations.idiomatic: When the Lin Shuangwen rebellion erupted, he took command of the campaign, but the army made no headway for a long time.

sentences.zh: 總督常青、李侍堯先後劾仕簡貽誤，奪官，逮下刑部論斬，特宥之。

translations.literal: Governors-General Chang Qing and Li Shiyao successively impeached Shirjian for causing delay and harm; he was stripped of office, handed over to the Board of Punishments for judgment of death, and specially pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Governors-General Chang Qing and Li Shiyao impeached him one after another for bungling the campaign; he was dismissed, sent to the Board of Punishments for a capital sentence, and then specially pardoned.

sentences.zh: 尋赦歸，卒。

translations.literal: Soon he was pardoned and returned home, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon pardoned and sent home, where he died.

sentences.zh: 仕簡子秉淳前卒，以其孫嘉謨襲爵。

translations.literal: Shirjian's son Bingchun had died earlier; his grandson Jiamo inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: Shirjian's son Bingchun had died before him, so his grandson Jiamo inherited the dukedom.

sentences.zh: 秉淳初授藍翎侍衛，累遷至狼山總兵。

translations.literal: Bingchun was first appointed a guard with blue plumes and rose step by step to Langshan regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: Bingchun began as a guard with a blue plume and rose to regional commander at Langshan.

sentences.zh: 嘉謨初授頭等侍衛，累遷至溫州總兵。

translations.literal: Jiamo was first appointed a first-class guard and rose step by step to Wenzhou regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: Jiamo began as a first-class imperial guard and rose to regional commander at Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: =穆赫林=穆赫林，博爾濟吉特氏，滿洲正藍旗人。

translations.literal: Mu Helin, of the Borjigit clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Mu Helin, a Borjigit Manchu of the Plain Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 祖瑣諾木，為兀魯特貝勒。

translations.literal: His ancestor Suonuomu was a beile of the Olot.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestor Suonuomu was a beile of the Olot Mongols.

sentences.zh: 太祖時，從明安來歸。

translations.literal: In the time of the Taizu Emperor, he followed Minggan in coming to submit.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taizu Emperor's reign he followed Minggan in submitting to the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 積戰閥，授二等總兵官。

translations.literal: Through accumulated military merit he was granted the second-rank post of regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: He built up a record of battle honors and was made a second-rank regional commander.

sentences.zh: 卒，順治間，追諡順良。

translations.literal: He died; in the Shunzhi reign he was posthumously given the title Shunliang.
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was posthumously given the temple name Obedient and Good during the Shunzhi reign.

sentences.zh: 再傳，子僧格襲世職，遇恩詔，累進三等伯。

translations.literal: After two generations, his son Senge inherited the hereditary office; on grace edicts he was repeatedly advanced to third-rank baron.
translations.idiomatic: Two generations later his son Senge inherited the hereditary post and, through successive grace edicts, rose to third-rank baron.

sentences.zh: 卒，穆赫林襲職。

translations.literal: He died, and Mu Helin inherited the office.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, Mu Helin inherited the post.

sentences.zh: 康熙五年，授正藍旗滿洲副都統，列議政大臣。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kangxi he was appointed vice commander of the Plain Blue Banner Manchus and listed among the deliberative ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Kangxi he became vice commander of the Plain Blue Banner Manchus and joined the ranks of deliberative ministers.

sentences.zh: 吳三桂反，十三年，偕都統拉哈達率兵駐防兗州，旋命移駐江寧。

translations.literal: When Wu Sangui rebelled, in the thirteenth year he together with Commander Lahada led troops to garrison Yanzhou and was soon ordered to transfer to garrison Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sangui rebelled, in the thirteenth year he and Commander Lahada garrisoned Yanzhou and were soon ordered to move to Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 時耿精忠叛應三桂，大將軍康親王杰書、將軍貝子傅喇塔討之。

translations.literal: At that time Geng Jingzhong rebelled in response to Sangui; Grand General Prince Kang Jieshu and General Prince Fuleta campaigned against him.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Jingzhong then rose in support of Sangui; Grand General Prince Kang Jieshu and Prince Fuleta were sent to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 穆赫林率所部喀喇沁、土默特兵赴浙江，與傅喇塔師會。

translations.literal: Mu Helin led his Khalkha and Tumed troops to Zhejiang and joined Fuleta's army.
translations.idiomatic: Mu Helin marched his Khalkha and Tumed troops to Zhejiang and joined Prince Fuleta's force.

sentences.zh: 十四年，從攻台州，精忠將林沖糾眾萬餘，列十三寨拒戰。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he followed the attack on Taizhou; Jingzhong's general Lin Chong gathered more than ten thousand men and arrayed thirteen stockades to resist.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he joined the assault on Taizhou, where Jingzhong's general Lin Chong mustered more than ten thousand men in thirteen fortified camps.

sentences.zh: 穆赫林督兵攻拔其寨，斬獲無算，复仙居。

translations.literal: Mu Helin directed troops to storm and take their stockades, slaying and capturing beyond count, and recovered Xianju.
translations.idiomatic: Mu Helin stormed the camps, killing and capturing beyond count, and recovered Xianju.

sentences.zh: 師自黃岩進，精忠將曾養性偕叛將祖弘勳據溫州分水陸迎戰，穆赫林擊敗之上塘嶺，得戰艦三十餘。

translations.literal: The army advanced from Huangyan; Jingzhong's general Zeng Yangxing together with the rebel general Zu Hongxun held Wenzhou and met the attack by land and sea; Mu Helin defeated them at Shangtang Ridge and captured more than thirty warships.
translations.idiomatic: The army advanced from Huangyan. Jingzhong's general Zeng Yangxing and the rebel Zu Hongxun held Wenzhou and met the attack by land and sea; Mu Helin routed them at Shangtang Ridge and seized more than thirty warships.

sentences.zh: 精忠將彭國明率眾五千瀕甌江列寨，穆赫林率兵至寶帶橋奮擊，斬級千餘，盡獲其槍械旗幟，遂薄江而陣，賊來犯，輒戰卻之。

translations.literal: Jingzhong's general Peng Guoming led five thousand men to camp along the Oujiang; Mu Helin led troops to Baodai Bridge and fought fiercely, beheading more than a thousand and capturing all their firearms, weapons, and banners; he then drew up close to the river, and whenever the bandits attacked he fought them off.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhong's general Peng Guoming lined up five thousand men along the Ou River. Mu Helin struck hard at Baodai Bridge, killed more than a thousand, and captured all their arms and banners; he then deployed along the riverbank and beat back every assault.

sentences.zh: 溫州繞城為壕屬甌江，為閘以蓄水，師爭閘，賊護甚力，久未能薄城。

translations.literal: Wenzhou was encircled by a moat connected to the Oujiang, with sluice gates to store water; the army contested the gates, but the bandits defended them fiercely and for a long time the army could not close on the city.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhou was ringed by a moat fed from the Ou River and fitted with sluice gates to hold water; both sides fought over the gates, the rebels defended them stubbornly, and for a long time the army could not press the walls.

sentences.zh: 時康親王杰書駐金華，檄傅喇塔與穆赫林速攻城。

translations.literal: At that time Prince Kang Jieshu was stationed at Jinhua and ordered Fuleta and Mu Helin to attack the city swiftly.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Kang Jieshu, then at Jinhua, ordered Fuleta and Mu Helin to take the city at once.

sentences.zh: 穆赫林言必得大砲乃可克。

translations.literal: Mu Helin said that heavy cannon would be necessary before it could be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Mu Helin said the city could not be taken without heavy cannon.

sentences.zh: 十五年，上責王貝子等遷延，師無功。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year the emperor rebuked the princes and others for delay, and the army achieved nothing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year the emperor rebuked the princes for dragging their feet, and the campaign still had nothing to show.

sentences.zh: 王因劾穆赫林與副都統吉勒塔布、提督段應舉等違令瞻顧狀，命事平議罪。

translations.literal: The prince therefore impeached Mu Helin, Vice Commander Jiletabu, Provincial Commander-in-Chief Duan Yingju, and others for disobeying orders and showing hesitation, ordering that their crimes be deliberated once affairs were settled.
translations.idiomatic: The prince then impeached Mu Helin, Vice Commander Jiletabu, Provincial Commander Duan Yingju, and others for disobeying orders and hanging back, with punishment to be decided after the campaign.

sentences.zh: 八月，康親王自衢州攻克仙霞關，精忠降，徙養性、弘勳等至福州，檄穆赫林移師福建，駐守延平。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Prince Kang advanced from Quzhou and captured Xianxia Pass; Jingzhong surrendered; Yangxing, Hongxun, and others were moved to Fuzhou; Mu Helin was ordered to transfer his army to Fujian and garrison Yanping.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Prince Kang took Xianxia Pass from Quzhou and Jingzhong surrendered; Yangxing, Hongxun, and others were sent to Fuzhou, and Mu Helin was ordered into Fujian to garrison Yanping.

sentences.zh: 鄭錦使其將吳淑、吳潛自邵武來攻，穆赫林擊之浦塘隘口，陣斬其將楊大任等，乘勝复邵武、汀州二府及所屬縣。

translations.literal: Zheng Jing sent his generals Wu Shu and Wu Qian to attack from Shaowu; Mu Helin struck them at Putang Pass, beheaded in battle his general Yang Daren and others, and following victory recovered the two prefectures of Shaowu and Tingzhou and their subordinate counties.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Jing sent Wu Shu and Wu Qian against him from Shaowu; at Putang Pass Mu Helin killed their general Yang Daren and others in battle, then swept on to recover Shaowu and Tingzhou and their counties.

sentences.zh: 錦屢犯泉州，复侵潮州，穆赫林與副都統沃申、總兵馬三奇等分兵赴之，屢捷。

translations.literal: Jing repeatedly invaded Quanzhou and again encroached on Chaozhou; Mu Helin together with Vice Commander Woshen, Regional Commander Ma Sanqi, and others divided troops to meet him and repeatedly won.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Jing repeatedly struck Quanzhou and raided Chaozhou; Mu Helin, Vice Commander Woshen, Regional Commander Ma Sanqi, and others divided their forces to meet him and won again and again.

sentences.zh: 十七年，錦犯海澄，穆赫林與海澄公黃芳世率兵迎擊於灣腰樹，戰失利，退保海澄。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Jing invaded Haicheng; Mu Helin and Duke of Haicheng Huang Fangshi led troops to meet the attack at Wanyao Tree, were defeated in battle, and withdrew to hold Haicheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Zheng Jing attacked Haicheng; Mu Helin and Duke of Haicheng Huang Fangshi met him at Wanyao Tree, were beaten, and fell back to defend the city.

sentences.zh: 錦复糾眾環偪，據高阜瞰城中，砲石交下，穆赫林與應舉協力固守，糧盡，身負重創，未幾城陷，乃與應舉自經死。

translations.literal: Jing again gathered masses to surround and press in, occupied high ground overlooking the city, and rained down cannon shot and stones; Mu Helin and Yingju jointly held firm in defense; provisions were exhausted and he suffered grave wounds; before long the city fell, and he then hanged himself together with Yingju.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Jing massed his forces, seized the heights above the city, and poured down shot and stones. Mu Helin and Duan Yingju held out together until grain ran out and Mu Helin was badly wounded; when the city soon fell, both men hanged themselves.

sentences.zh: 事平，吏議穆赫林徵溫州師無功，守海澄聞援且至，不能突圍出，當奪官及世職，籍其家，上以穆赫林有戰功，貰籍沒，命其從子赫達色襲爵。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled, the officials deliberated that Mu Helin, in the campaign against Wenzhou, had achieved nothing; in defending Haicheng, though he heard relief was about to arrive, he could not break out, and therefore his office and hereditary rank should be removed and his household registered for confiscation; the emperor, because Mu Helin had military merit, remitted the confiscation and ordered his younger clansman Hedase to inherit the title.
translations.idiomatic: After peace returned, officials judged that Mu Helin had failed at Wenzhou and, though relief was near during the siege of Haicheng, had not broken out; he should lose office, hereditary rank, and property. The emperor, weighing his earlier battle honors, spared confiscation and had his clansman Hedase inherit the title.

sentences.zh: 世宗時，詔與應舉併入祀昭忠祠。

translations.literal: In the time of the Shizong Emperor, an edict ordered that he and Yingju together be entered for worship in the Shrine of Manifest Loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Yongzheng Emperor an edict enrolled him and Duan Yingju together in the Shrine of Manifest Loyalty.

sentences.zh: =段應舉=段應舉，漢軍鑲藍旗人。

translations.literal: Duan Yingju was a Han Bannerman of the Bordered Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Yingju, a Han Chinese bannerman of the Bordered Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 父思信，明廣寧千總。

translations.literal: His father Sixin was a battalion commander of Guangning under the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sixin had been a Ming battalion commander at Guangning.

sentences.zh: 太祖取廣寧，來降，予世職備禦。

translations.literal: When the Taizu Emperor took Guangning, he came to submit and was granted a hereditary office for frontier defense.
translations.idiomatic: When the Taizu Emperor captured Guangning he surrendered and was given a hereditary frontier-defense post.

sentences.zh: 卒，應舉襲。

translations.literal: He died, and Yingju inherited.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, Yingju inherited the post.

sentences.zh: 從端重親王博洛討叛將薑瓖，攻汾州及太谷，克之。

translations.literal: He followed Prince Duanzhong Bolo in suppressing the rebel general Jiang Xiang, attacked Fenyang and Taigu, and captured them.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Prince Duanzhong Bolo against the rebel Jiang Xiang, took Fenyang and Taigu, and captured both.

sentences.zh: 復從貝勒屯齊徵湖南，屢有功。

translations.literal: He again followed Prince Tunqi in campaigning in Hunan and repeatedly had merit.
translations.idiomatic: He later served under Prince Tunqi in Hunan and distinguished himself repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 累擢鑲藍旗漢軍梅勒額真，進世職二等阿達哈哈番。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to meyendargen of the Bordered Blue Banner Han Army and advanced in hereditary office to second-rank adaha gūsai.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to meyendargen of the Bordered Blue Han Banner and was advanced in hereditary rank to second-class adaha gūsai.

sentences.zh: 偕鎮國將軍王國光赴廣東，駐防潮州。

translations.literal: He together with Prince of the State Wang Guoguang went to Guangdong and garrisoned against the tide at Chaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He went to Guangdong with Prince of the State Wang Guoguang and was stationed on coastal defense at Chaozhou.

sentences.zh: 康熙三年，剿叛將蘇利於南塘鋪，賊敗遁，复碣石衛。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kangxi he suppressed the rebel general Su Li at Nantangpu; the bandits were defeated and fled, and Jieshi Guard was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Kangxi he routed the rebel Su Li at Nantangpu; the enemy fled and Jieshi Guard was recovered.

sentences.zh: 敘功，進世職一等。

translations.literal: When merits were recorded, his hereditary office was advanced to first rank.
translations.idiomatic: For his service his hereditary rank was raised to first class.

sentences.zh: 尋署山東提督。

translations.literal: Soon he acted as Shandong provincial commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He soon served as acting Shandong provincial commander.

sentences.zh: 十三年，率兵赴杭州剿禦耿精忠，授福建提督。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he led troops to Hangzhou to suppress and defend against Geng Jingzhong and was appointed Fujian provincial commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he marched to Hangzhou against Geng Jingzhong and was appointed Fujian provincial commander.

sentences.zh: 擊賊仙居、黃岩、太平、樂清，進圍溫州，皆捷。

translations.literal: He attacked bandits at Xianju, Huangyan, Taiping, and Yueqing, advanced to besiege Wenzhou, and was victorious in every case.
translations.idiomatic: He fought through Xianju, Huangyan, Taiping, and Yueqing and pressed the siege of Wenzhou, winning every engagement.

sentences.zh: 十五年，從康親王徵福建，精忠降。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he followed Prince Kang in campaigning in Fujian, and Jingzhong surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he followed Prince Kang into Fujian, and Geng Jingzhong surrendered.

sentences.zh: 時鄭錦據漳、泉、興化，與將軍拉哈達合兵進剿，復興化、泉州二城。

translations.literal: At that time Zheng Jing held Zhangzhou, Quanzhou, and Xinghua; together with General Lahada he combined forces to advance in suppression and recovered the two cities of Xinghua and Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Jing still held Zhangzhou, Quanzhou, and Xinghua; Yingju joined General Lahada, advanced against him, and recovered Xinghua and Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 復分兵定漳州及海澄等縣，應舉進駐海澄。

translations.literal: He again divided troops to pacify Zhangzhou and counties including Haicheng, and Yingju advanced to garrison Haicheng.
translations.idiomatic: He then split his forces to secure Zhangzhou and counties including Haicheng, and Yingju moved in to garrison Haicheng.

sentences.zh: 十七年，劉國軒、吳淑等陷平和，穆赫林戰失利，詔責應舉不能平賊，調江寧提督楊捷代之，應舉仍以副都統從征。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Liu Guoxuan, Wu Shu, and others took Pinghe; Mu Helin was defeated in battle; an edict rebuked Yingju for being unable to pacify the bandits, transferred Jiangning provincial commander-in-chief Yang Jie to replace him, and Yingju still followed the campaign as vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Liu Guoxuan and Wu Shu took Pinghe and Mu Helin was beaten; the court blamed Yingju for failing to finish off the rebels, replaced him with Jiangning commander Yang Jie, and kept Yingju on campaign as a vice commander.

sentences.zh: 尋城陷，死之。

translations.literal: Soon the city fell, and he died for it.
translations.idiomatic: When the city soon fell, he died defending it.

sentences.zh: =【論】=論曰：鄭氏為海疆患三十餘年，捷、正色扞衛艱難，內定泉、漳，外收金、廈；

translations.literal: Commentary: The commentary says: The Zheng clan was a scourge on the maritime frontier for more than thirty years; Jie and Zhengse defended through hardship, pacifying Quanzhou and Zhangzhou within and recovering Kinmen and Xiamen without;
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: The Zheng family plagued the coast for more than thirty years. Yang Jie and Wan Zhengse bore the brunt of the defense, pacifying Quanzhou and Zhangzhou inland while recovering Kinmen and Xiamen at sea;

sentences.zh: 英、理遂佐施琅越海恢疆，而理尤忠奮，稱虎將。

translations.literal: Ying and Li then assisted Shi Lang in crossing the sea to recover territory, and Li was especially loyal and spirited, called a tiger general.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Ying and Lan Li then helped Shi Lang cross the sea to recover the coast, and Li in particular was so loyal and fierce that men called him a tiger general.

sentences.zh: 方鄭氏亂時，有自海上降者，輒優以封爵，林興珠為建義侯，鄭鴻逵為奉化伯，周全斌為承恩伯，鄭纘緒為慕恩伯，梧最先降，授成功舊封。

translations.literal: During the disorder of the Zheng clan, those who surrendered from the sea were promptly favored with enfeoffment: Lin Xingzhu became Marquis of Jianyi, Zheng Hongkui Baron of Fenghua, Zhou Quanbin Baron of Chengen, Zheng Zuoxu Baron of Muen; Wu surrendered first and was granted Chenggong's old enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zheng rebellion, defectors from the sea were generously ennobled: Lin Xingzhu as Marquis of Jianyi, Zheng Hongkui as Baron of Fenghua, Zhou Quanbin as Baron of Chengen, Zheng Zuoxu as Baron of Muen. Wu was the first to surrender and received Chenggong's former title.

sentences.zh: 子芳世殉漳州，以忠延世。

translations.literal: His son Fangshi died martyred at Zhangzhou, extending the lineage through loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fangshi died for the cause at Zhangzhou, and loyalty carried the line forward.

sentences.zh: 穆赫林等死海澄，孤城抗節，亦自有足稱者。

translations.literal: Mu Helin and others died at Haicheng, holding an isolated city with steadfast integrity—they too had merit enough to be praised.
translations.idiomatic: Mu Helin and the others who died at Haicheng held a lone city to the end; that too deserves honor.

sentences.zh: 悍寇死戰，御之艱，克之尤偉矣！

translations.literal: With fierce bandits fighting to the death, defending against them was arduous—conquering them was all the more magnificent!
translations.idiomatic: Against enemies who fought to the death, defense was hard—but victory was all the more glorious!
